Committed on `day/dttrade`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The four changed games, first divergence each (every one a held attacker now declared):** game 77 (turn 35) — the user seat's Solphim, Mayhem Dominus (5/4) and Sheoldred, the Apocalypse (4/5 deathtouch) attack ai1 at 35, whose one untapped creature is its commander Atraxa (4/4 deathtouch); base: no attack (both "eaten for nothing" by the clause). Atraxa blocked Solphim, both died, Sheoldred connected for 4 — the deathtouch commander traded down. Better. Game 42 (turn 20) — Trophy Mage (2/2) joins Bruce Banner against the user at 5 life, whose only blocker is Roadkill Rodney (2/1 deathtouch): Rodney blocking it is a near-even trade (5.2 against 3.9 value), not a free kill. Rodney blocked it, Tamiyo's Safekeeping saved it, Rodney died. Better. Game 50 (turn 23) and game 71 (turn 31) — a lone 3/3 Elephant token against a group whose safe attacker it can trade with up (Solitude 3/2; Vihaan, Goldwaker 3/3, the commander): its best block is that trade, so the small attackers it could otherwise eat (Bloom Tender and Generous Pup; Zulaport Cutthroat) cost nothing more — one blocker, one block. Both times the Elephant blocked that attacker and the extras connected (3 and 1 more damage). Better under the model, and the engine's defender behaved as it predicts. Game 71's winner change comes 12 turns later (the game is 10 turns shorter), not attributable to the one point.
> · **The census** (every AI declaration through a pure hook in scratch copies of both trees — 80 / 80 byte-identical to the clean runs on each): declarations into an untapped deathtouch creature that can block the attacker **35 → 37**; of them, attackers bigger (power plus toughness) than every such blocker — the boards the clause called free kills — **2 → 5** (power 10 → 21: + Trophy Mage, Solphim, Sheoldred). Deathtouch blockers are rare in this batch: 16 combats (base) offer an attacker one can block — Atraxa in 29 of the 35 declarations — so the batch exercises the fix only lightly; the witnesses carry it.
> · **The gap** (opponentAI.outnumberingAttackers, 221d4fb4): `worstCaseLoss` matched blocker slots only to "killers" — blockers that kill the attacker for nothing by `blockKillsForNothing`, whose deathtouch clause counts a mutual kill as free when the attacker is bigger — and credited nothing for the blocker that dies; a non-deathtouch trade counted nothing at all.
> · **The fix** — `opponentAI.tradeLossPrefixes` (new; `tradeEdgeValue` the edge, `combatDuel` decides who dies): the loss of each cheapest-first prefix of the attackers (those that go anyway first) is the defender's maximum-weight matching of slots to attackers under edges worth LIFE_PER_VALUE × (the attacker's value if it dies − the blocker's value if it dies), floored at 0. Exact: the Hungarian method adds one row at a time and keeps the matching of the rows so far optimal (dual feasible, tight on matched edges, unmatched columns at potential 0), so one pass gives every prefix, O(R²·(S+R)); the bound — up to 64 matching rows, beyond which the base (the attackers that go anyway) is bounded from below by a greedy matching and every longer prefix from above (the smaller of each slot's best edge and each row's best edge summed), so the gain is never overstated. A menace / "≥N" attacker is N rows of 1/N its best single-blocker trade (worstCaseLoss's reading). The damage side is unchanged (`unavoidableDamage`, every slot chumping the biggest), both worst cases at once. Policy `racerTrade: "v1"` keeps `worstCaseLoss` (POLICY_KEYS); test handle `__tradeLossPrefixesForTests`. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.8 describes it.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) The damage stays off the edges. A single assignment whose edges also carry the damage a block stops would charge a chump its blocker and so assume the defender chumps; then a small attacker it would eat for free looks cheap — `opponentAI.test.js` "drops unprofitable attackers" (a 5/5 and a 1/1 into a 3/3 wall at 10 life) went red that way, sending the 1/1 to die. Kept: damage and loss at the defender's best, both at once, as the racer already judged. (2) First draft valued a menace attacker's gang block (the N strongest blockers together killing it, no blocker loss charged) — an upper bound that, on an attacker going anyway, inflated the base and made the group look free: run 1 of the A/B changed a fifth game (48: Tempestra, Big Mother Mouser and Tokka & Rahzar sent beside Heroes in a Half Shell into Bruce Banner and Abomination, both of which eat them for free) for that reason alone. Revised to worstCaseLoss's single-blocker reading, and the over-cap bound made one-sided; game 48 is byte-identical in the run of record. (3) Trades are valued by `boardEval.permanentValue` (mana value heavy): Old Gnawbone (13.2) for a commander Atraxa (9.4) is a 15.2-life loss, so Gnawbone joins a wide attack into Atraxa only when what else Atraxa could block is worth more than that (the witness: four Grizzly Bears beside it, Atraxa's controller at 9), and stays home at 40 (a control). (4) A trade with a non-deathtouch blocker now counts when the attacker is worth more (it counted nothing): the effect seen in games 50 and 71.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) `unavoidableDamage` (opponentAI.js:2621) ignores trample and double strike — the racer's lethality, the group's damage, the walker policy's reach and the crack-back all read it; separable, but it moves lethal calls everywhere and needs its own A/B. (2) The per-attacker hold still uses the clause (`blockKillsForNothing`, opponentAI.js:2595): the racer's safe set and the planeswalker policy's `safe` filter (opponentAI.js:3268) still treat a bigger attacker into a smaller deathtouch blocker as eaten for nothing — the group judgment now rescues the racer's, the walker policy's is not. (3) Gang blocks (two blockers on one attacker) are modelled on neither side, menace included (opponentAI.js:2867). (4) A blocker with lifelink gains its controller life on the block (Atraxa: 4), not valued. (5) A blocker that can block several attackers is read as independent slots, each charged its death (blockSlots' reading), so blocking two attackers it is charged twice.
> · Witness: `aiRacerDeathtouchTrade.test.js` (16).

> ## 🔧 2026-10-20 — FIX (AI decision quality + soft-lock): the session driver's anti-loop latch no longer throws away an action that changed the game — it read only `progressSignature` (turn, step, distinct attackers / blockers, stack depth, the active player's hand and pool, battlefield count, the free-cast / cascade / discover windows) and passed from the state before any auto-decided non-pass action that moved none of those, so every AI crew while crew took effect at once (22 of 22 in the 80-game A/B), a turn-face-up paid by tapping lands (CR 701.40b), a second block by a creature that can block more than one (CR 509.1a — Palace Guard) and "done" in Etali, Primal Storm's cast-from-among window (CR 608.2g — the window never closed and the game wedged) were undone; now `antiLoopLatch.actionChangedGame` reads the signature first and then the whole state outside the bookkeeping fields, with exact repeats folded, so PR 10.3's re-declared-attacker loop and a true no-op are still passed on · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,769 unchanged
> Suite **21,795 green (1 skipped) / 1,945 files** under the gate queue, first run (with the rules index built for the run inside the worktree, then deleted); it ran on the final code and test bytes (sha256 of the four changed code and test files checked before and after the run) — the docs (this entry, CHANGELOG, ENGINE-SCAFFOLD) were written beside it, and no test reads them. Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of 12,493 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,504 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0** (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of 660c7639; native-* + land 15,769 of 34,584 snapshot names on both). **Mutants 6/6** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256): the whole-state read removed (5 tests red — the four witnesses and the predicate's change cases), repeats not folded (2 — PR 10.3's loop control), the log compared (2 — the no-op control), the priority holder and pass count compared (1), an undefined-valued key counted (1), a rebuilt object counted as a change (3). Witness `antiLoopLatch.test.js` (6) run on the untouched 660c7639 archive: **the 4 witnesses fail there on assertions, the 2 controls pass on both**; it was written beside the engine change, not before it. `antiLoopLatchProgress.test.js` (2) pins the predicate. A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 660c7639 archive): **74 byte-identical**; **6 change play** — games 60, 63, 64, 65, 66, 69, the Shorikai Vehicles pod — and **every first divergence is an AI crew the base threw away** (Prodigy's Prototype, Imposter Mech as a copy of Thrun, Breaker of Silence, Shorikai, Nautiloid Ship, Mechtitan Core, Smuggler's Copter); crew-vehicle log lines 0 → 12; **1 winner changes** (game 69, ai2 → ai3); turns move in 4 (60: 36 → 32, 64: 33 → 35, 65: 47 → 32, 69: 57 → 51); 0 errors, 0 engine-stuck, 0 turn-cap games on either tree (longest game 62 turns / 3,197 ticks on both); results unchanged (ai-wins 53 / user-wins 27); **196.2 s / 193.1 s (24.46 / 24.86 games per minute)**. The predicate's cost, timed as an observer over the 80 games: 9,747 calls, 70.1 ms in all (about 7 µs a call); the whole-state read ran 12 times. Committed on `day/latch`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The latch and its history.** PR 10.4 (5972d3da, 2026-06-05) added it behind PR 10.3's fix (b9570788): a Vigilance attacker stayed untapped after its declaration, was offered again, and each re-declaration appended another copy of the same attacker entry — the signature counted DISTINCT attackers for exactly that. 1beabb4a (2026-07-01) added the pending-window bits after the latch rolled a free-cast decline back to a force-pass on the pre-decline state and wedged the window — the same failure as this one, fixed then for three flags only.
> · **The census** (observer hooks in a copy of the base tree, the 80-game batch byte-identical to the plain base run): 9,811 auto-decided non-pass actions; **22 left the signature unchanged, all `crew-vehicle`, all real changes** (the crew taps, `becameTappedThisTurn`, `pendingTapEvents`, a layer-4 continuous effect, a summoning-sick stamp) — Prodigy's Prototype ×3, Shorikai ×7 (Shimmer Myr, Kotori, Ironsoul Enforcer crewing), Imposter Mech-as-Thrun ×2, Nautiloid Ship ×2, Mechtitan Core ×4, Smuggler's Copter ×4, in games 60, 63–66, 69; **no true no-op**. On the fixed tree the same census found **0 of 9,747** non-pass actions with an unchanged state. Outside the batch, a static read of the dispatcher's 23 handlers found three more signature-blind actions, each reproduced on the base through the driver: turn-face-up paid by tapping lands (no stack, nothing enters or leaves, the pool 0 → 0), a multi-blocker's second block (same `blockerId`), and `cast-from-among-done` (clears `pendingCastFromAmong`, a flag the signature never read — on the base the AI's Etali exiled only a Day of Judgment it holds, the window stayed open, and no seat was offered anything but the window until the user's turn-19 cleanup). The signature also reads only the ACTIVE player's hand and pool, so a non-active seat's tap-for-mana or instant-speed suspend was invisible to it.
> · **The fix** (`antiLoopLatch.js`, a new zero-import leaf; `learnSession.js` imports it and drops its private copy of `progressSignature`). `actionChangedGame(before, after)`: identical objects → no change; a different signature → change (the common case, unchanged cost); otherwise the whole state is compared, skipping `LATCH_BOOKKEEPING_KEYS` (`log`, `priorityHolder`, `consecutivePasses`, `idSeq`, `timestampCounter`, `rngSeed` — every action restates the priority fields, CR 117.3c, and the counters move only beside a change seen elsewhere), treating an undefined-valued key as absent, and comparing arrays with exact repeats removed (first occurrences, order kept): a duplicated attacker entry and the duplicated defender in the attacker's `attackedPlayersThisTurn` memo are PR 10.3's loop and stay "no change"; a new, removed, changed or reordered element is a change. The latch site is otherwise as it was: a no-change action is replaced by a pass from the state before it.
> · **On master 39b8a81a** (crew on the stack): `learnSession.js` is byte-identical on 660c7639 and 39b8a81a, and the change applies cleanly there. Crew now pushes a stack object, so the signature already sees it — the latch keeps it with or without this fix, and the whole-state read never runs for a crew. On a 39b8a81a archive with this change: `antiLoopLatch`, `antiLoopLatchProgress`, `activationPriority`, `crewVehicles`, `mobilizerMech`, `termination`, `freeCast` — 7 files, 62 tests green; on pure 39b8a81a the crew witness passes and the turn-face-up, multi-block and Etali witnesses fail.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) the signature stays as the fast path — a different signature is always a different state, so it changes no outcome, and it keeps the whole-state read off ~99.9% of actions. (2) Repeats fold at every array, not only `combat.attackers`: the re-declaration also grows the attacker's per-turn defender memo, so a combat-only dedupe would have kept PR 10.3's loop alive to the tick budget. (3) The two control loops are reconstructed with module mocks (the pre-PR-10.3 attacker offer; a dispatcher that answers the AI's land drop with a rebuilt state and a log line), since neither loop can occur on the current engine. (4) No true no-op turned up in either census, so none is named as latched; the controls stand in for the class.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) The decision-trajectory row for an auto-decided action is recorded before the dispatch (`resolveDecideAction`, learnSession.js:2612 → the row write at :1145), so a latched no-op still leaves a row whose action never happened — 0 such rows in the 80 games after the fix, 22 (the crews) before. (2) While a cast-from-among / free-cast / cascade / discover window is open, every other seat is offered nothing (legalChoices.js:4765 and its siblings) — correct mid-resolution, but it is why a window that never closes wedges the whole table rather than one seat.
> · Witness: `antiLoopLatch.test.js` (6), `antiLoopLatchProgress.test.js` (2).

> ## 🔧 2026-10-20 — FIX (rules faithfulness, false positive): ward triggers on a TRIGGERED ability an opponent controls (CR 702.21a — "Whenever this permanent becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, counter that spell or ability unless that player pays [cost]") — the trigger-target entry's found-not-fixed (2): ward was raised for spells and activated abilities only, so an opponent's triggered ability aimed at a ward permanent resolved without the ward cost ever being demanded (Ravenous Chupacabra destroyed a Leonin Lightbringer for free); now the flush and the person's trigger-target answer record it on the ability and the session driver asks it — the existing soft-counter pay-or-be-countered question — before anyone receives priority; the AI's trigger chooser passes over a ward it won't pay while another correct-side target is free of it · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,769 unchanged
> Suite **21,801 green (1 skipped) / 1,944 files** under the gate queue, first run (the rules index built in the worktree's app/data for the run, then deleted; no MTG_APP_ROOT in that job); it ran on the final code and test bytes (sha256 of src/lib/learn, src/components/mtg and src/hooks, aeb407ce…, checked before and after the run and again before the commit) — the docs (this entry, CHANGELOG, ENGINE-SCAFFOLD, PLAY-API-CONTRACT) were written beside it, and no test reads them. Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of 12,500 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,510 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0** (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of 660c7639; native+land 15,769 of 34,584 snapshot names on both). **Mutants 7/7** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256; run in a scratch copy of the tree): the flush records no ward (7 tests red), the person's answer records none (2), the driver never asks (9), the record not cleared as it is asked (5), the ward asked before the trigger-target question (1), the chooser ignoring a ward it won't pay (1), ward.js taxing the controller's own permanent (2 — the controls). Witness `wardTriggeredAbility.test.js` written before the engine change and run on the untouched 660c7639 archive in its final form: **14 tests — 10 fail there on assertions, the 4 controls pass on both** (your Bond Beetle's counter on your own Lightbringer, chosen by you; the AI's Bond Beetle on its own Lightbringer; Murder at the opponent's Lightbringer asks the ward exactly as before; the AI's Chupacabra at a creature without ward). A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 660c7639 archive): **80 / 80 byte-identical** (the sha256 of every game record — each decision row, the log, result, winner, turns, ticks), 0 errors on either tree, results unchanged (ai-wins 53 / user-wins 27), 198.5 s / 195.3 s. **Census** (scratch copies of both trees instrumented with one log line per new triggered ability aimed at an opponent's ward permanent, evaluated where the after tree records the ward; each instrumented batch equals its uninstrumented twin once those lines are dropped, 80 / 80 on both; the instrumentation seen to fire on a Chupacabra-at-Lightbringer probe on both trees): **0 on base, 0 after** — 19 ward cards in the 30 decks (printed or granted: Innkeeper's Talent, Sheltered by Ghosts, Chains of Custody, Brotherhood Regalia), 14 of them entered the battlefield, 42 (card, game) pairs, and spells were asked a ward 8 times in the base batch (Swords to Plowshares at a ward-granted Walking Ballista, Path to Exile at Ghyrson Starn, Valorous Stance at Hexing Squelcher …), but no triggered ability in the batch aimed at one. (An 8-game smoke run of the A/B script — one game per pod, meant as a zero-game load check — ran ungated before the gated runs; its output was discarded.) Committed on `day/wardtrig`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The gap** (660c7639): `actionDispatcher` raised ward at the cast path (wardTaxForSpell → setPendingSoftCounterChoice, :1155) and the activated-ability path (:1864); `gameEngine.flushTriggers`' target-event loop (:2351) and `settleTriggerTargetChoice` ran becomes-the-target, crime and Kira only. ward.js's header already claimed "an opponent's ABILITY targeting a ward permanent now raises the ward tax too" for triggered abilities.
> · **The fix** — reuse, not a second ward: `markWardOwed` (after Kira, in the flush loop and in the settle) asks `ward.wardTaxForStackObject` — the cast and ability paths' detector (one ward target; the mana, life and discard costs; an opponent's permanent only) — and stamps `wardOwed: { cost, wardName }` on the triggered ability; `raiseWardOwed` (the session driver, right after the trigger-target raise, before the pendingChoice block) turns the lowest owed ability into the existing `soft-counter` pause (`setPendingSoftCounterChoice` → `resolveSoftCounterChoice`, `autoPickSoftCounterPay` for an AI, the SoftCounterPanel for a person) and clears the record. `chooseTriggerTargets` gains `withoutUnpaidWard` (ahead of the loop backstop, the fight restraint and the flicker pick): a correct-side candidate whose ward its controller wouldn't pay (the same answer the driver will give) is dropped while another candidate is free of it; all such → unchanged. The stack view (boardSnapshot.stackView) whitelists fields, so `wardOwed` never reaches the board. PLAY-API-CONTRACT's `soft-counter` row now says spell or ability (no new kind, no shape change, PLAY_API_VERSION unchanged). ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.4 names it.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) RECORDED at the flush and ASKED by the driver, not raised in the flush: the choice slot is single (setPendingSoftCounterChoice no-ops when occupied) — raising in the flush would have dropped a second ward in one batch and, on the cast path, the spell's own ward (raised after its cast-trigger flush; witnessed: Murder + Weaver of Lightning's ping at one Lightbringer ask {2} twice), and a flush inside a resolution never sets a choice. (2) The ward is asked as an immediate pay-or-counter, as the spell and ability paths model it — no ward object on the stack that players could respond to. (3) Order: the spell's ward before its cast trigger's; within one batch the lowest owed ability first. In the rules a cast trigger's ward goes on the stack after the spell's and resolves first — only a payer short of mana for both sees a difference. (4) The ward is asked only after every ability of its batch has its targets (the driver raises the trigger-target question first — CR 603.3: the batch goes on the stack before the wards that trigger on it); an explicit gate in raiseWardOwed was removed as dead code (its mutant survived — the driver order already guarantees it; the mutant swapping that order is the one kept). (5) The chooser preference is small and ranking-only (never a wrong-side target); it shares the AI's pay-if-able answer, so the AI never aims where it will then decline. (6) A caller that resolves the stack without the session driver skips an owed ward (as every ward did before for triggers); resolveTopOfStack does not refuse it, unlike `awaitingTargets`, since AI previews resolve copies without the driver.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **Loyalty abilities raise no ward** — `applyActivateLoyalty` (actionDispatcher.js:2011–2091) runs becomes-the-target, crime and Kira but never `wardTaxForStackObject` (Chandra, Torch of Defiance's −3 at a ward creature is free). (2) Every ward settle resets priority to the active player (learnSession.settleSoftCounterChoice :754 → gameEngine.finalizeStackResolution :1308 → resetPriorityLoop :222), so a non-active caster loses the priority it keeps after casting (CR 117.3c) — spells and activated abilities before this slice, now triggers too. (3) `autoPickSoftCounterPay` (effects/runProgram.js:1718) pays whenever able — including for a forced trigger that harms its own controller's side (a mandatory buff forced onto an opponent's ward creature). (4) A spell or ability with two or more ward targets raises no ward (ward.js:138 — each is its own trigger; safe FN, unchanged). (5) `parseWardCost` reads "Ward—Discard a card or pay {2}" (Titania, Rugged Rumbler) as discard only and "Ward—Discard a card at random" (Alpharael, Stonechosen) as a chosen discard (ward.js:100). (6) A redirect onto a ward permanent (change-target — effects/runProgram.js:1955 moveStackTarget) and a copy with new targets raise no ward. (7) The SoftCounterPanel says "<card> will be countered" for an ability too (learnDecisionPanels.jsx:1699).
> · Witness: `wardTriggeredAbility.test.js` (14).

> · **The gap** (gameEngine.buildTriggerStack / chooseTriggerTargets, 31d97587:1620–1646): one chooser picked the targets of every seat's triggered abilities; a person's "destroy target creature an opponent controls" or "2 damage to any target" was aimed by the AI's heuristic, an "up to one" could not be declined, and a modal trigger's mode was the AI's. Both earlier ledger entries named it found-not-fixed (the trigger-target restraint entry, (2); the reflexive-trigger entry, Faebloom Trick's tap).
> · **The fix** — the ability goes on the stack WAITING for its controller (CR 601.2a: an object is on the stack while its choices are made). At a live flush (`flushTriggers` with the automatic chooser) a trigger of a seat in `state.humanSeats` (createLearnSession stamps the user seat below Expert) is routed with `askControllerChooser`: with two or more legal candidates, or a modal "choose up to one" with any, it answers the private `ASK_CONTROLLER` sentinel at each of `buildTriggerStack`'s four choose sites (intervening-if, non-modal, modal, reflexive), and the ability is put on the stack in its APNAP place with its payload, no target yet, and `awaitingTargets: { candidates, abilityText, allowNone? }` — the engine's own `expandCastChoices` candidates, legality never re-derived. Its target events (becomes-the-target, crime, Kira) are skipped there. The session driver, before the pendingChoice block, raises the question for the LOWEST waiting object (`raiseTriggerTargetChoice` → `setPendingTriggerTargetChoice`, the new `trigger-target` kind — the order the batch went on the stack, CR 603.3b). `settleTriggerTargetChoice` writes the pick where the chooser writes it (`targets`, `payload.params.targets` / `.chosenMode`), runs the target events, and once no object of the batch waits flushes what they enqueued (together, APNAP). "none" removes a modal "choose up to one" ability (CR 603.3c, 700.2b); an answer that is no candidate decides nothing and is asked again. `resolveTopOfStack` throws on a waiting object — the driver asks before anyone receives priority. A single legal choice is taken unasked, as before. Contract: `PENDING_CHOICE_KINDS` + fixture (auto path `autoPickTriggerTarget` — the chooser's pick among the waiting object's choices, mapped to its index), `PLAY_API_VERSION` 1.4.0 (PLAY-API-CONTRACT.md row), the wire whitelist gains `abilityText` and `allowNone`; the board snapshot never shows `awaitingTargets`. UI: `TriggerTargetPanel` (learnDecisionPanels.jsx — one button per legal choice: a target by name and whose, a player by seat, "No target" for the decline, a mode by its text, "Choose no mode" for allowNone), `useLearnSession.applyTriggerTargetChoice`, the LearnView sheet and router. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.4 names it.
> · **One existing test changed:** `auraEntryHostChoice.test.js` — its Displacer Kitten and Brago triggers are the person's, so the person now answers their targets first (`aimTrigger`, the same permanents the automatic chooser took) before the Aura's host question; the "AI flicker read" case now asserts that the automatic answer to the person's Brago question is the set a table without a person blinks (brago, rancor, vis). 23/23 green.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) waiting on the stack, not pausing the flush mid-batch: every flush site's own follow-up (hold in declare blockers when the stack grew, the cleanup window, the attack-declaration hold, a resolution already paused on another choice) stays exactly as it is, and the settle is local to one object. (2) Modal triggers are in: their candidates are (mode × targets) already, so the person chooses the mode too (CR 603.3c) — Knight of Autumn's three modes, each labelled. (3) The AI's triggers later in APNAP order choose their targets at the flush, before the person answers — the rules have them choose after the person's are on the stack; only a "target an ability on the stack" choice could differ. (4) The ask fires only at a live flush (`chooseTargets === chooseTriggerTargets`), so a caller passing its own chooser — tests, the AI's cast-time preview (`entersTriggerRemovesOwn`, which calls `buildTriggerStack` directly) — is untouched. (5) An answer that names no candidate re-asks rather than picking for the person.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **No order choice for a person's simultaneous triggers** — CR 603.3b lets each player put theirs on the stack "in any order they choose"; `orderTriggersAPNAP` (gameEngine.js:1398) keeps FIFO within a controller, for every seat. (2) **Ward never triggers on a triggered ability's target** — `flushTriggers`' target-event loop (gameEngine.js:2351, and now the settle) runs becomes-the-target, crime and Kira only; ward's pay-or-be-countered is raised for spells and activated abilities in the dispatcher (actionDispatcher.js:1864), never for a triggered ability, for any seat. (3) The expander's 64-candidate cap (targeting.js:91; the "up to one" decline appended last at :462) drops a person's decline past 63 legal targets and limits "any number" (Brago) to 64 subsets — with 7+ nonland permanents a person can't pick every subset. (4) A person's single-candidate OPTIONAL ability whose one target is on the wrong side still becomes the Arbiter no-op (askControllerChooser gameEngine.js:1439 → chooseTriggerTargets → `pickForcedTriggerCandidate` returns null for an optional atom, :1962) instead of going on the stack with that target and asking "you may" at resolution — false-negative safe. (5) A trigger the α1 allowlist sends to the Arbiter no-op (an atom whose target side can't be read — gameEngine.js:1774) is never offered to a person either.

> · **The bug (reproduced on 32865c89, the engine's own entry points).** Two seats, the user's Grizzly Bears attacking the AI's Hill Giant, the
>   user holding Giant Growth: in declare blockers the user held priority with no block (Giant Growth offered), passed; the AI declared its
>   block and passed — and the step ended (`first-strike-damage` next). In a pod (the user attacking ai2) the order was user (no block) → ai1 →
>   ai2 blocks → ai3 → step over: neither the attacker nor ai1 ever saw the block in the step. The phantom first-strike damage step (found,
>   not fixed (2)) was the only window where a human attacker could still pump; the AI's block-trick reader (`trickGain`) asks for the declare
>   blockers step, so the AI attacker never did.
> · **The fix** (`gameEngine.js`, `gameState.js`, `legalChoices.js`). Entering declare blockers marks `combat.blockDeclarationOpen`
>   (`runStepActions`; `gameState.blockDeclarationOpen` is the one predicate). While it is open `legalActionsForPlayer` offers only
>   `declare-blocker` and the pass — no spell, ability, special action or mana ability (CR 509.1: no player has priority during the turn-based
>   action). `passPriority`: when the lap completes with the declaration open it calls `closeBlockDeclaration` instead of resolving or
>   advancing — the block triggers fire (`fireBlockTriggers`, shared with `nextStep`'s forced advance; the mark goes, `_blockTriggersFired`
>   set) and the active player gets priority, passes 0 (CR 509.2, 509.2a). The close happens once, so the next full lap with an empty stack
>   ends the step — no loop. `actionsDeclareBlocker` returns nothing once `_blockTriggersFired` is set: before this gate the fixed tree offered a
>   block in 463 post-close windows of the 80 games (the AI took none), now 0; the base offered one whenever a block trigger held the step (the
>   witness shows it on the archive; no such window came up in the 80 base games). The
>   reset is not in `applyDeclareBlocker`: a block is one action of the declaration, and a per-block reset would hand priority around between
>   two blocks of one defender, leave the no-block case without the attacker's window, and still fire the block triggers after it. A state
>   with neither mark (a test built inside the step, an older save) keeps the older shape. The wrong citation on the old `nextStep` comment
>   ("CR 509.4" — a creature put onto the battlefield blocking) is now 509.2a.
> · **Census (AI decisions in declare blockers, the observed runs; base → after).** Attacker windows with blocks declared **13 → 273** (43 with a
>   cast offered), attacker casts there **0 → 6** (the six above); defender casts after its blocks 2 → 2 (game 54's Tamiyo's Safekeeping on
>   Laboratory Maniac now comes after the attacker's pass, same log; game 52's left with that game's divergence; game 43's Tyvar's Stand is new,
>   downstream); during the declaration (after) 1,339 attacker / 1,674 defender / 1,957 other windows, 0 casts offered; the base's attacker
>   windows before any block (1,343, 201 with a cast offered) cast nothing, so no cast was lost. Karametra's Blessing was never offered to an
>   attacker after blocks in the 80 games. Unchanged: first-strike damage step casts 1 → 1, combat damage step 16 → 16.
> · **Steps checked for a missing pass-count reset.** Declare attackers: the active player declares while holding priority with the count at 0
>   and its closing pass counts as its priority (CR 508.2) — correct. Combat damage, first-strike damage, end of combat: `grantPriority`
>   resets — correct. Resolution: `resetPriorityLoop` — correct. Dispatcher handlers: play-land, cast, activate, hand self-put, cycle,
>   discard-ability, plot, turn-face-up, loyalty, companion, suspend reset; the mid-resolution declines (discover, free cast, cascade, cast from

> · **The measurement** (the A/B of record's base, the first declaration tick of every combat censused through a pure hook in a scratch copy — 80 / 80 byte-identical to the untouched archive): 1,495 combats; in 468 the racer held an attacker some blocker of the focused player could kill for nothing (swing not lethal). In **160 of them (65 games)** a one-blocker-per-attacker count allowed more: more offered attackers survive a joint assignment (the offered attackers less a maximum matching of them to blockers that kill them for nothing) than were declared — 1,388 power held; the declared attackers' worst-case face damage over the 468 was 582, every offered attacker's 1,399. Most of those holds are right: the attacker a blocker would eat is a commander, a mana creature or a utility creature (Kinnan, Omnath, Thrasios, Elvish Mystic into one 3/3; Veyran into Zaxara's deathtouch) worth more than the damage the rest add. > · **The gap** (opponentAI.selectProfitableAttackers, 79bbb347): the W4 hold sent an attacker only when it was unstoppable or no single eligible blocker killed it for nothing (`attackerDiesForNothingV2`), each judged against every blocker at once; lethality alone overrode it. The racer weighed no crack-back (the brief assumed it did): a creature it held stayed home as a blocker by accident.
> · **The fix** — `opponentAI.outnumberingAttackers` (new), called by `selectProfitableAttackers` after the hold when the swing is not lethal (policy `racer: "v1"` keeps the hold; POLICY_KEYS). The held attackers facing the focused player itself, power above 0, never a land (its permanentValue reads 0; it dies a mana source), sorted cheapest first (`boardEval.permanentValue`, power, id); the group is the cheapest k beside the attackers that go anyway (declared, the racer's safe ones, the creatures that must attack — `requiredAttackerIds`, now read before the racer). Gain = face weight × (unavoidableDamage(group) − unavoidableDamage(the rest)) − LIFE_PER_VALUE × (worstCaseLoss(group) − worstCaseLoss(the rest)): damage with the defender blocking the biggest blockable attackers with every blocker slot (`blockSlots`: one per untapped creature, more under "can block an additional creature" / "any number", `combatEvasion.maxBlocksFor`), loss with its blocks killing the most valuable attackers they can (`worstCaseLoss`: a one-slot matching to the blockers that kill each for nothing, greedy by value — exact, a transversal matroid — and a fractional knapsack of menace / "≥N" attackers over the slots, the smaller kept; CR 509.1a, 702.111b); both worst cases at once, which no single block achieves — conservative. LIFE_PER_VALUE = 4 (evaluateBoard's 0.25 per life point; the walker policy's WALKER_LIFE_PER_VALUE now reads it), the face weight 20 / life below 20 (FACE_URGENCY_LIFE). The best k with gain > 0 whose crack-back is not lethal (`crackBackReader`: each living opponent's creatures that can attack — defender, "can't attack" excepted — blocked biggest-first by the AI's creatures still untapped, an attacker without vigilance staying tapped, CR 508.1f, 702.20b; summed over the opponents) and whose attack taxes the seat can pay with the attackers that go anyway paid first (`attackTaxDetail` at the face, `canAfford` from the sources less the attackers that tap, CR 508.1h, 508.1i). `pickAttackPlan` declares the group last, cheapest first, so each per-tick re-plan counts the declared ones in and reproduces the rest. `blockKillsForNothing` is factored out of `attackerDiesForNothingV2`, unchanged. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.8 names it.
> · **Judgment calls:** the exchange rate is evaluateBoard's, so five Grizzly Bears into one Rumbling Baloth at 40 life stay home (8 damage < a Bear's 12.8) and attack when its controller is at 10; five 2/2 tokens go (a control and two witnesses pin it). A block that kills a bigger attacker while its smaller deathtouch blocker dies too stays "for nothing", as the per-attacker hold counts it. The crack-back guard covers only the added group; the racer's safe attackers keep their old behaviour.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) A trade with a smaller deathtouch blocker is valued as a free kill: `blockKillsForNothing` (opponentAI.js:2197) keeps the per-attacker rule, and `worstCaseLoss` credits nothing for the blocker that dies — game 78's Old Gnawbone (9/9), Avenger of Zendikar (5/5) and Apex Devastator (10/10) stayed home against Atraxa (4/4 deathtouch), which dies blocking any of them; valuing it as a trade needs an edge-weighted matching. (2) The planeswalker policy's attacker filter is still per attacker: `planWalkerAttacks`' `safe` (opponentAI.js:2735) asks whether any one of the walker controller's blockers kills it for nothing. (3) Only the focused player's face: `chooseDefender` (opponentAI.js:2544) picks the target first; a group held there is never weighed against an opponent with fewer blockers. > · **Taxes** — `costTaxForSpell(taxers, spell, caster, activePlayer)`: an `exceptCasterTurn` tax (Defense Grid) skips a spell cast on its caster's own turn — the Grid's controller pays it on an opponent's turn too ("each spell"); with no active player named the tax applies (the full cost, never a discount). > · **Scaled reducers** carry `per` with `amount: 0` until stamped, so a reader that never resolves the scale reduces nothing. Per counter on the source (`perCounterOnSource` — "… counter on this creature/artifact", the self-name normalized upstream): `collectCostReducers` stamps it off the permanent's own counters (Animar's ruling witnessed through a real cast: the cost is fixed before its cast trigger adds a counter). Per board count (`perEachCount`): `resolveCastSiteReducers` counts it for the caster through `countForSpec` at the cast site (layer-aware power — a Grizzly Bears with two +1/+1 counters counts for Temur Battlecrier), and drops a `duringYourTurn` reducer on another player's turn. Only `parseCountSource`'s `permanentsYouControl` counts with no `who` and no `excludeSelf` are admitted (the cast site has no source to exclude — "for each other creature you control" stays unread). "<filter> spells you cast have affinity for artifacts" is the same lane over artifacts you control (CR 702.41a; 702.41b — two Samis both apply). Sokka counts himself (his ruling).

> · **The bug** (reproduced on 92356a54). The damage pipeline and the toughness atoms ran `destroyLethalCreatures` (and, for planeswalkers, `destroyZeroLoyaltyPlaneswalkers`) inside the resolution, right after their own step, with the dies triggers queued there: `spellEffects.applyDamageEffect` (spellEffects.js:1846/1849), `dealSimultaneousDamage` (1679), the pump / animate / earthbend / pump-pair / base-P/T atoms (effects/atoms/combat.js:429, 507, 545, 820, 2938, 3003), and the counter, token, manifest, persist, amass and clone entries below. `runEffectProgram` puts an instant or sorcery into its owner's graveyard only after the last atom (`finishSpellResolution`, CR 608.2n), so every death was judged before it — and before every later step. Probed: a 2/3 Tarmogoyf dies to Bolt (ruling: survives as 3/4); Last Gasp kills it (ruling: "or lowers its toughness" — 0/1, survives); Ember Shot at the caster's 3/3 Psychosis Crawler kills it before "Draw a card" makes it 4/4; Marauding Raptor's rider read an empty battlefield after its own damage killed the Dinosaur; Swift Demise's "Then destroy" found nothing to destroy.
> · **The rules** (bundled CR, cited exactly). CR 704.3 / 117.5 — state-based actions are checked whenever a player would receive priority; CR 704.4 — "state-based actions pay no attention to what happens during the resolution of a spell or ability"; CR 608.2n — an instant or sorcery is put into its owner's graveyard as the final part of its resolution; CR 608.2c — the instructions are followed in the order written; CR 704.5f / 704.5g — toughness 0 or less, lethal damage; CR 704.5h / 702.2b — a creature dealt damage by a deathtouch source "since the last time state-based actions were checked" is destroyed; CR 704.5i — a planeswalker with loyalty 0.
> · **The fix** — `gameState.openResolutionWindow` / `closeResolutionWindow` (a transient `resolutionWindow` flag): `resolveTopOfStack` opens it before the resolver runs, `finalizeStackResolution` closes it just before its `checkAllStateBasedActions`. `destroyLethalCreaturesAfterEffect(state, deathtouched, cause)` is the check an effect runs: outside the window it is `destroyLethalCreatures` (unchanged — costs, special actions, combat damage, direct calls, the AI's simulations on a copy of the board such as `triggerTargetRestraint`'s fight read, which runs at the flush after the window closes); inside it destroys nothing and adds the deathtouched creatures to `deathtouchedSinceSba`, which `sba.checkAllStateBasedActions` takes into its lethal pass (CR 704.5h) and clears. `destroyZeroLoyaltyPlaneswalkersAfterEffect` does the same for the damage path's loyalty check. Neither field exists at a priority checkpoint or in a save (no schema change). ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.5 names the rule for a new effect.
> · **Call sites moved** (23 — 22 lethal checks and one loyalty check; all `destroyLethalCreatures(…)` → `destroyLethalCreaturesAfterEffect(…)` unless named): spellEffects.js:1680 (`dealSimultaneousDamage` — fights, bites), 1850 + 1854 (`applyDamageEffect` + its loyalty check); effects/atoms/combat.js:430 (pump), 508 (animate), 546 (earthbend), 821 (pump-pair), 2939 (set-base-pt-team), 3004 (set-base-pt-target); effects/atoms/counters.js:189 (-1/-1 counters), 266 (proliferate); effects/atoms/distributeCounters.js:108 (put-leave-counters-on-self), 137 (move-all-counters); effects/atoms/manifest.js:81; effects/atoms/selfReturn.js:427 (persist); effects/atoms/tokens.js:332, 369, 796, 1314; effects/atoms/amass.js:110; resolvers.js:488 (a clone with nothing to copy entering), 395 (`resolveCloneChoice`, a settle) and effects/runProgram.js:1262 (`resolveDistributeChoice`, a settle) — the two settles run after a pause, outside the window, so they still destroy at once; converted so they follow the rule if a pause ever keeps the window. **Left as they were** (not inside a resolution): combatResolution.js:831/834 (combat damage — the check right after it is the one before priority), combatResolution.js:131 (the end-of-combat delayed removals, applied without the stack), actionDispatcher.js:1753 / 2081 (a cost's counter removal and a loyalty cost, CR 601.2h), actionDispatcher.js:2397 (turning a manifest face up, a special action), urDragonAttack.js:102 (an attack trigger applied without the stack), sba.js:236/240 (the check itself).
> · **Reach.** Probed through a real Lightning Bolt cast against each Tarmogoyf-class card with a creature card and a sorcery card in the graveyards (no instant): Tarmogoyf, Polygoyf, Barrowgoyf, Pyrogoyf, The Duke of Midrange and Chimney Goyf die on 92356a54 and survive here as 3/4 (all six sized); Nethergoyf and Consuming Blob count their controller's graveyard, so an opponent's Bolt still kills them (correct — the spell goes to its caster's graveyard); Cognivore and Magnivore change when the spell is an instant / a sorcery (the Cognivore/Shock witness). Beyond the CDAs every death a spell or ability causes now happens after it (log order; by reading, the deaths of several steps of one resolution are now one batch at one check, CR 704.3, so the leaves and dies look-backs of P·34 and 1571b5e4 see one event), and any later step reads the creature still on the battlefield: Swift Demise and Marauding Raptor in the A/B; the hand-count CDAs under a spell that damages then draws (Psychosis Crawler witnessed; Tishana, Voice of Thunder, Body of Knowledge and Maro by the same reading).

(2) The session loop's check also runs while a resolution is paused (learnSession.js:1566, before the pending choice is surfaced), as does its player-loss check. (3) Two state-based actions are still performed at the move inside a resolution: an Aura whose host left goes to the graveyard at once (CR 704.5m, gameState.detachPermanentFromAll, gameState.js:1662) and a token that leaves the battlefield ceases to exist at once (CR 704.5d, gameState.js:926) — a later step of the same resolution that reads them would differ (no case found). (4) **AI decision quality:** the AI's kill read for a damage or shrink spell uses the toughness before the spell's own card joins a graveyard (e.g. opponentAI.js:435, the X-damage picker: `xOf(a) < tou`), so it can now Bolt a 2/3 Tarmogoyf expecting a kill it no longer gets (before, the engine killed it). > · **The measurement** (the A/B of record's base, every `pickAttackPlan` call censused through a pure hook in a scratch copy — 80 / 80 byte-identical to the untouched archive): 1,496 combats, 3,125 declarations, **0 combats with an opposing planeswalker offered**, so 0 attacks at one — not the planner: 25 of the batch's 26 planeswalker casts resolved as `spell-unresolved` ("planeswalker (unmodeled static/triggered ability)") and the 26th was countered. With loyalty carried (the supplement's base): 26 combats offered a planeswalker (Tamiyo, Field Researcher 13, Sarkhan, Fireblood 4, Vraska the Unseen 3, Ajani Steadfast 3, Sorin Markov 3, Teferi, Hero of Dominaria 1, Kaya, Orzhov Usurper 1; loyalty 1–10, mostly 4); in 21 the offered attackers could kill one under the worst case, in 10 with the racer's safe attackers only; in 4 a walker could fire its ultimate next turn; in 18 its controller was the focused player, in 5 it had no untapped creature (the only boards the old focus read). The AI attacked a planeswalker in 4.
> · **The gap** (opponentAI.pickAttackPlan, 9a5238ef): PW-3's `chooseWalkerToKill` diverted only when the walker's controller had NO untapped creature, sent the whole chosen swing at the highest-loyalty walker, never used a creature the racer held back from the focused player, never looked at an ultimate, and re-planned each tick from the attackers still undeclared — so a kill needing two attackers lost its second after the first was declared (the supplement's game 20: one Sarkhan attacker declared, the other sent at the player; Sarkhan survived to the next turn). `selectProfitableAttackers` also counted an attack already declared at the focused player's planeswalker toward the player's lethal sum.
> · **The fix** — `opponentAI.planWalkerAttacks` (new), read by `pickAttackPlan` for every offered creature while a planeswalker is offered (pools narrowed by `obeyingAttackOptions` as before — a goaded creature never goes at one while a player other than the goader is free, CR 508.1d, 701.15b). Never while the swing is lethal on the focused player (`faceSwingIsLethal`, swingIsLethalV2 over the creatures that face that player). Per walker: `walkerThreat` — loyalty, value = 4 × `boardEval.permanentValue` (evaluateBoard's 0.25 per life point), the ultimate (the most expensive loyalty cost above the printed starting loyalty) and `ultimateNext` (loyalty already pays for it: its controller fires it on their next turn, CR 606.3, and only damage removes loyalty before then, CR 306.8). Goals: the kill (need = loyalty; worth = value, twice that with the ultimate due) and, with the ultimate due, bringing it below (need = loyalty − ultimate + 1; worth = value). `cheapestReach` picks the attackers giving up the least face damage whose damage connects beside those already declared at the walker when its controller chump-blocks the biggest blockable ones with every untapped creature (`unavoidableDamage`, factored out of swingIsLethalV2 unchanged — block legality, menace and "≥N"); an attacker counts only when that controller's blockers can't kill it for nothing (the racer's `attackerDiesForNothingV2`); its cost is the power it would have dealt the focused player (0 when the racer wasn't sending it), weighted by 20 / life below 20 life. A goal goes ahead when worth > cost and its taxes are paid: every planned attack at a walker pays `attackTaxDetail(state, controller, walkerId)`, summed across walkers and funded by `canAfford` from the seat's sources less the planned attackers without vigilance (CR 508.1f, 508.1i), Phyrexian pips with `lifePaymentContext` as the offer pays them. Greedy by gain across walkers. The walker attacks lead the plan (each pays its tax before a face attack spends the mana); everything else keeps the racer's face target. `selectProfitableAttackers` leaves attacks at the defender's planeswalkers out of its committed lethal sum. Policy key `walker: "v1"` restores the old focus and sum (POLICY_KEYS). ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.8 names the policy.
> · **The supplement's three games**: game 20 (turn 17) — both 2-power attackers at Sarkhan, Fireblood (4, no blockers), which dies (base: one, then the other at the player). Game 55 (turn 28) — ai2's 4-power attacker that ai3's one untapped creature can't block kills ai3's Tamiyo, Field Researcher (4), the other attacker goes at the focused ai1 (base: both at ai1; Tamiyo was offered in 7 more combats, to turn 40). Game 78 (turn 36, no blockers) — Omnath's Old Gnawbone (7) at Atraxa's Ajani Steadfast (6) and Omnath (2) + Surrak and Goreclaw (7) at Sorin Markov (9, its −7 due next turn); Maze of Ith untapped Gnawbone and prevented its damage, so Sorin alone died (base: Ajani died, Sorin lived and reached 10).

The same enrichment feeds `/api/learn/start` (route.js:52, :98) — not checked in the running app. Carrying the field (the supplement's patch) lets 12 of 23 casts enter and changes 11 of the 80 games against the untouched base; it is its own change. (2) The racer's per-attacker "dies for nothing" hold ignores that one blocker stops one attacker (`selectProfitableAttackers` / `attackerDiesForNothingV2`, opponentAI.js:2280, :2185): in the supplement Omnath kept 13 creatures (34 power) home on turns 32 and 34 of game 78 against Atraxa's single untapped creature, and the planeswalker policy inherits it — Sorin Markov at 7 with its −7 due went unattacked on turn 34. > ## 🔧 2026-10-18 — FIX (user-facing): a planeswalker's printed loyalty survives deck enrichment — every planeswalker in a game deck was a no-op cast · **±0**
> Found by the planeswalker-attack slice: in the 80-game A/B batch 25 of 26 planeswalker casts resolved as `spell-unresolved` and the 26th
> was countered. Cause: `learnDeckEnrich.mergeCardData` copied power and toughness from the local index but never `loyalty`, and the
> already-shaped branch (the app's saved-deck snapshot) backfilled only layout and colour identity — so `startingLoyalty` read null,
> `planeswalkerPlayable` refused the card, and actionDispatcher routed the cast to SPELL_NOOP. The same enrichment feeds `/api/learn/start`,
> so the Academy had it too (by reading). Fix: `mergeCardData` carries `loyalty` (a card's own is never overwritten), and the shaped branch
> backfills a missing loyalty on a Planeswalker type line (CR 306.5b). Witness `learnDeckEnrichLoyalty.test.js` (5): the 2 witnesses fail
> on the base on assertions, the 3 controls pass on both; mutants 3/3 (merge drops it, no backfill, overwrite own) each restored
> byte-identical. Not covered: a transforming card whose planeswalker face is the back face (the index's top-level loyalty is the front
> face's; game decks carry no card_faces) — its own slice with the exile-and-return-transformed entry.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-18 — FIX (false positive / rules faithfulness): a creature with a printed `*` toughness whose characteristic-defining ability the engine models dies to lethal damage and to toughness 0 like any other creature (CR 704.5g, 704.5f; CR 208.2, 604.3, 613.4a) — the Apex Altisaur entry's found-not-fixed (1): Lumra, Bellow of the Woods carried 190 damage in that repro and, with no lands, stayed on the battlefield as a 0/0; all 73 sized creatures of the corpus's 184 printed-`*`-toughness creatures (Tarmogoyf, Master of Etherium, Boneyard Wurm, Dakkon Blackblade, Crusader of Odric, Ulvenwald Hydra …) were immortal to damage and -X/-X. The layer engine now says whether it computed a toughness (`toughnessSized` — a printed number, a modeled layer-7a CDA or a layer-7b set; a 7d switch swaps it with power's) and the state-based action skips only the 111 it can't size — none of them credited native · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,660 unchanged
> Suite **21,461 green (1 skipped) / 1,920 files** under the gate queue (with the rules index built for the run, then deleted) — run 1, the green of record; the docs (this entry, CHANGELOG, ENGINE-SCAFFOLD) were written beside it — no test reads them. Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of 12,171 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,477 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0** (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of 4f5ccd5e, snapshotted before the first edit; native+land 15,660 of 34,584 snapshot names on both). **Mutants 6/6** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256): the old printed-number guard back (11 tests red), no skip at all (3 — the two unsized controls and the switched Coiling Woodworm), a 7a CDA that doesn't size (10), a 7b set that doesn't size (1), a 7d switch that doesn't swap the sized flags (2), the no-effect fast path always sized (3). Witness `starToughnessSba.test.js` (21), written before the engine change and run on the untouched archive: **14 fail there on assertions, the 7 controls pass on both** (Lumra at 2 damage, Tarmogoyf at 2 damage, an indestructible Darksteel Juggernaut under lethal damage, Boneyard Wurm at 2/2, the unsized Treefolk Seedlings and Souls of the Lost under 1 damage, Grizzly Bears). A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 4f5ccd5e archive): **77 byte-identical, 3 change picks**, 1 winner changes — all three in the Shorikai Vehicles pod, all Master of Etherium now destroyed by lethal damage it was dealt (it never died in the 80 base games): game 64 (turn 29, Thrun, Breaker of Silence fights it through Ulvenwald Tracker — winner Shorikai Vehicles → Thrun Voltron), game 68 (turn 23, it blocks a trampler and dies in combat; winner unchanged), game 69 (turn 22, Ancient Animus's fight; winner unchanged); results unchanged (ai-wins 57 / user-wins 23), 0 errors on either tree (236.8 s / 286.5 s). Lumra was not cast in these 80 games. Committed on `day/startough`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The bug** (reproduced on 4f5ccd5e). `destroyLethalCreatures` skipped every printed creature whose printed toughness is not a number (`if (printedCreature && !Number.isFinite(Number(perm.card?.toughness))) continue;`), before both checks. The skip exists because `ptPrimitive` reads a printed `*` as 0: a creature whose CDA is unmodeled would die to a toughness it never had. But it skipped the creatures the layers DO size too. A census over the bundled corpus (each creature on a board with five Forests and a Grizzly Bears, 99 damage marked, the state-based check run): **0 of the 184** printed-`*`-toughness creatures died on base; 72 of the 73 sized ones die after (Darksteel Juggernaut is indestructible), none of the 111 unsized.
> · **The rules** (bundled CR, cited exactly). CR 208.2 / 208.2a — a `*` is set by a characteristic-defining ability; CR 604.3 — a CDA defines power or toughness; CR 613.4a — layer 7a applies it; CR 613.4b — layer 7b sets; CR 613.4d — 7d switches power and toughness; CR 704.5f — toughness 0 or less puts a creature into its owner's graveyard (indestructible doesn't stop it); CR 704.5g — lethal damage destroys it (CR 702.12b — indestructible does).
> · **The fix** — `layers.applyLayer7` tracks `powerSized` / `toughnessSized`: a printed number, a 7a `ptSetDynamicCount` that sets the value, or a 7b set (fixed or counted, gate open); a 7d switch swaps them. `deriveCharacteristics` carries both (the no-effect fast path from the printed value, the empty record false); `permanentToughnessSized(state, id)` reads it. `destroyLethalCreatures` skips a printed creature only while its toughness is unsized; an animated noncreature keeps its derived-value read. A layer-1 copy reads the copiable card for the printed value, as the derive does. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.6 names the signal.
> · **Coverage (CREED).** No card loses credit: all 46 native printed-`*`-toughness creatures are sized (the classifier's static lane credits a clause through `clauseProducesStatic` — the same `parseClause` the layers read), and all 111 unsized ones are body-only. The census places an adventurer by its permanent face (`adventure.permanentFaceCard`, what a cast puts onto the battlefield): Beanstalk Giant and Cruel Somnophage are sized as cast (probed through a real cast). The witness pins the lockstep on seven real cards (five sized-and-native, two unsized-and-not).
> · **Reach.** Changes behaviour for 72 cards — 45 credited native: Nethergoyf, Flora Colossus, Revenant, Harmonious Grovestrider, Lhurgoyf, Master of Etherium, Dakkon Blackblade, Beanstalk Giant, Psychosis Crawler, Cantivore, Mortivore, Dungrove Elder, Nightmare, Serpent of the Endless Sea, Ulvenwald Hydra, Broodstar, Tarmogoyf, Tishana, Voice of Thunder, Slag Fiend, Overbeing of Myth, Battle Squadron, Seraph of the Masses, Polygoyf, Squelching Leeches, Boneyard Wurm, Braulios of Pheres Band, Body of Knowledge, Magnivore, Scion of the Wild, Cognivore, Lumra, Bellow of the Woods, Cruel Somnophage, Soramaro, First to Dream, Sturmgeist, Molimo, Maro-Sorcerer, Multani, Maro-Sorcerer, Wayfaring Temple, Uktabi Wildcats, Splinterfright, Geist-Honored Monk, Crusader of Odric, Maro, Mirkwood Pathmaker, Burrowguard Mentor, Terravore; and 27 body-only whose body the engine plays (Ashaya, Soul of the Wild, Titania, Gaea Incarnate, Old Man Willow, Cultivator Colossus, Kalonian Twingrove, Barrowgoyf …). A switched creature (Twisted Image) takes the sized-ness of the value it takes: Treefolk Seedlings switched now dies to damage at its printed power, and an unmodeled-power `*`/1 (Coiling Woodworm) switched is no longer destroyed by the 0 it takes as toughness. Profile decks: Earth Bent (Lumra, Ashaya), Teval, the Balanced Scale Test (Lumra), Shorikai Vehicles (Master of Etherium).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **The Tarmogoyf ruling, newly exposed:** the bundled ruling says an instant or sorcery that damages Tarmogoyf "is put into its owner's graveyard before state-based actions are performed", so its card type can raise Tarmogoyf's toughness first. The engine runs the lethal pass INSIDE the spell's resolution (`spellEffects.applyDamageEffect`, spellEffects.js:1846; the -X/-X debuff at effects/atoms/combat.js:820), before the card moves. Probed after the fix: Tarmogoyf at 2/3 (a creature and a sorcery in the graveyards) dies to Lightning Bolt — by the ruling it is 3/4 when the check happens and survives; with an instant already in a graveyard it is 3/4 before and survives. Before this fix it survived every Bolt. Reach: the CDAs that count instant or sorcery types in graveyards — Tarmogoyf, Polygoyf, Barrowgoyf, Pyrogoyf, The Duke of Midrange, Chimney Goyf, Nethergoyf and Consuming Blob (own graveyard), Cognivore, Magnivore. (2) The 111 unsized `*` creatures are still never destroyed by toughness (the protective skip) — all body-only: a toughness-only CDA has no parser arm (staticAbilityParser.js:4041–4062 reads the Goyf, both-values and power-only shapes — Treefolk Seedlings), nor an ability-word-prefixed one (Souls of the Lost's "Fathomless descent —"), nor most "on the battlefield" counts (Plague Rats, Coiling Woodworm). (3) An adventurer's COMBINED card placed straight onto the battlefield (the census's first pass) read unsized — toughness 0 with five lands — while a cast gives the creature face, which is sized; not root-caused (whether any put-onto-the-battlefield path carries the combined card was not checked). (4) By reading, a layer-1 "becomes a copy" of a CDA creature (becomeCopy — Sarkhan, Soul Aflame's class) does not apply the copied CDA: `collectContinuousEffects` reads `staticEffectsOf(state, perm)` off the permanent's own card (layers.js:1175), not its copiable values — such a copy is now unsized and skipped where before it was checked against the stand-in 0 and died. (5) **AI decision quality:** the AI casts a sized `*` creature into a count of 0 — probed, `opponentAI.pickAction` (unchanged by this slice) picks Boneyard Wurm with two Forests and no creature cards in its graveyard, as it does with two — and the Wurm now enters as a 0/0 and dies at once (before, it sat there as an immortal 0/0). No A/B game cast one into a zero count.

> · **The bug** (re-proved on 68d2a979 by rebuilding the supplement's game 37 alone). The α1 chooser (`gameEngine.chooseTriggerTargets`) takes the first correct-side candidate, and the expander lists an "up to one" decline LAST (targeting.js — "real targets come BEFORE the decline"), so an optional fight was always taken, against the first legal creature. Jurassic Ramp's Apex Altisaur was indestructible there; Earth Bent's Lumra, Bellow of the Woods (23/23, a CDA) took 10 damage a fight and never died — the lethal-damage state-based action skips a printed `*` toughness (found-not-fixed (1)) — each fight dealt the Altisaur 23, its enrage put the fight back on the stack, and the game burned the per-turn raw tick ceiling. Away from loops the same pick lost games: a plain Altisaur fought a 15/15 and died to it; Kogla fought whatever came first.
> · **The rules** (bundled CR, cited exactly). CR 115.6 — an ability that requires targets may allow zero to be chosen; CR 601.2c — a variable number of targets is announced, the choice the ability's controller makes as it goes on the stack (CR 603.3d). CR 701.14a/b — each fighter deals damage equal to its power; nothing fights if either is gone. CR 704.5g / 702.12b — lethal damage destroys, indestructible ignores it. CR 104.4b — "Loops that contain an optional action don't result in a draw"; CR 732.4 — only a loop of mandatory actions is (mandatoryLoop.js: an untargeted LINK chain — this loop is neither); CR 732.3 — in a fragmented loop a player "must then make a different game choice so the loop does not continue"; CR 732.2a — a shortcut names a number of iterations.
> · **The fix** — `triggerTargetRestraint.js` (new; gameState, layers, triggers, triggerRouting, the parser and effects/atoms/combat — no import of gameEngine), two restraints `chooseTriggerTargets` applies to its correct-side candidates. (1) `restrainOptionalFights`: each candidate's source-bound "fights up to one target" (atom `fight` + `optionalTarget`, the enchanted-host form too) is read by `fightWorthTaking`, which resolves the fight on a copy of the board with `fightCreature` itself (so indestructible, deathtouch, protection, prevention, infect, regeneration and the lethal pass all count) — taken when the target leaves and the fighter stays; or, both alive, as a chain step: the fighter was dealt damage, its own self "is dealt damage" trigger fights (routing natively — Apex Altisaur's enrage), the target is not indestructible and still has toughness left, and at this fight's rate it runs out first (an indestructible fighter never does). Every other candidate becomes its decline, synthesized from the first candidate when the expander's 64-candidate cap cut the decline off. Each chain step re-reads the live board, so a chain lasts only while the target's remaining toughness falls (82 toughness, 9 fights). (2) the LOOP BACKSTOP (`loopSpent` / `loopBreakingChoice`): once `abilityResolutionsThisTurn` (the per-turn ledger resolveTopOfStack keeps, keyed by source + sentence) holds `LOOP_ITERATIONS` (300) for the trigger's ability, the next choice declines its optional targets, else takes a candidate aimed only at players. 300 clears the busiest legitimate turn measured (236 resolutions of one ability — the Squirrel turn in learnSession's tick-budget note) and is a few thousand ticks under the 20,000 raw ceiling. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.4 names the module.
> · **The human seat.** A triggered ability has no human target prompt: the chooser targets it for both seats (buildTriggerStack, gameEngine.js:1620–1646), so a person can't decline an "up to one" trigger target themselves (nor choose one) — found-not-fixed (2); with this fix their Apex Altisaur declines the same fights the AI's does.
> · **Reach** (bundled Commander-legal cards whose trigger routes natively): an optional source-bound fight 11 — Apex Altisaur (enters + enrage, the one enrage fighter), Kogla, Pheres-Band Brawler, Mind Meanderer, Wicked Wolf, Gargos, Vicious Watcher, Thorn Mammoth, Markov Enforcer and the Auras Pitiless Fists, Warbriar Blessing, Meltstrider's Resolve; self "is dealt damage" reflectors that can hit a creature 5 — Spitemare, Boros Reckoner, Needletooth Raptor, Red Hulk, Ill-Tempered Loner. Profile decks: Jurassic Ramp (Apex Altisaur), Omnath, Locus of Mana and Test Rashmi (Kogla), Zaxara (Gargos), Wolverine (Meltstrider's Resolve).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **A creature with a printed `*` toughness never dies to lethal damage or to 0 toughness** — `destroyLethalCreatures` skips it before both checks (gameState.js:2926, `if (printedCreature && !Number.isFinite(Number(perm.card?.toughness))) continue;`), even when the layers size it: Lumra (23/23) carried 190 damage in the repro; probed on 68d2a979, Lumra at toughness 3 with 9 damage and at toughness 0 (no lands) both stay on the battlefield. Every */* CDA creature the engine sizes (Lumra, Tarmogoyf, Lhurgoyf, …) is immortal to damage and -X/-X — a false positive; the guard exists because an UNSIZED CDA reads toughness 0, so the fix needs a "sized" signal from layer 7a. (2) No human target prompt for triggered abilities (above). (3) The two-target "target creature you control fights up to one target creature you don't control" triggers (fight-pair — Favored Enemy, Yoshimaru, Amok Time, Arni Slays the Troll, Gimli's Reckless Might, Tolsimir) are not read: the first pair is still taken (no self-retrigger, so no loop). (4) A MANDATORY targeted loop with a single legal target each (two indestructible Needletooth Raptors, nothing else to target) is, by reading, a CR 104.4b draw that `mandatoryLoop.js` misses — its LINK rule takes only untargeted triggers — and the backstop has no different choice there; the tick ceiling still ends it engine-stuck. (5) A "you may" loop (CR 603.5, decided as it resolves — the autopilot takes every "may") is outside the backstop. (6) CR 732.3 names the active player (or the first involved in turn order) as the one to change; the backstop changes whichever ability reaches 300 first. (7) By reading, the expander's 64-candidate cap also drops the "up to one" decline from a person's spell targets (targeting.js:91 `MAX_CAST_EXPANSIONS`, the decline appended last at :462).
> · Witness: `optionalFightLoop.test.js` (19); `fightDamagePipeline.test.js` +1 (the decline) and its Kogla/Dawn Elemental witness re-pointed.

Committed on `day/gylookback`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The bug.** `checkLeavesTriggers` offered each leave event to the leaving permanent itself and to the battlefield only (triggers.js:8160–8163 at 68d2a979); a watcher that left in the same event was in neither. Measured on the archive: Akroma's Vengeance with Marionette Apprentice and an Ornithopter drains 0 (either battlefield order); Wicked Visitor with a Glorious Anthem 0; Titania with a Dryad Arbor (Day of Judgment) no Elemental; Evacuation with Nadier's Nightblade and two Servos 0; Rat King and a Bears bounced make 1 Rat. The bundled rulings: Marionette Master (2016-09-20) "If Marionette Master and an artifact you control are put into a graveyard at the same time, Marionette Master's ability triggers."; Disciple of the Vault (2020-08-07) — it "triggers for that artifact".
> · **The fix — departed watchers look back** (`triggers.departedLeaveSources` / `departedSaw`, the twin of P·34's `deadLookBackSources`). Each leave in a drain is offered to the drain's departed watchers that SAW it: the watcher was on the battlefield as it left — every leave event now records `boardBeforeIds`, the battlefield immediately before it (`gameState.recordLeaveEvent`, from the `before` board the exit already passes) — or both left in ONE event. The engine moves a wipe's permanents one at a time, so the board a later member left no longer holds an earlier one: `gameState.groupLeaveEvents(state, ids)` marks the members of one event with a shared `group` before the drain — `applyDestroyEffect` (every destroy: wipes, multi-target, Culling Ritual, Blood Money), `applyZoneMove` (mass bounce / exile / tuck), `applyBlink`'s exile, `costSacrifice.sacrificePermanentsTogether` (group sacrifices, Living Death, N-permanent costs) and every `checkDiesTriggers` death batch (SBA lethal damage, combat). A watcher that left in an earlier, separate event never sees a later leave (witnessed both ways with two separate moves). A permanent still on the battlefield stays the sweep's — never twice.
> · **The battlefield sweep is gated the same way:** a watcher not on that board never saw the leave — a flickered permanent is back as a NEW object (CR 400.7). On the archive Ghostly Flicker on Ninth Bridge Patrol and a Bears put two counters on the returned Patrol (it "saw" the Bears and its own old object leave); now the departed Patrol triggers once and its counter has nowhere to go. Emblems, an orphaned Aura's leave and a leave recorded without the board (synthetic test entries) keep the old offer.
> · **Orphaned Auras** (CR 704.5m): the engine moves an Aura whose host left at once; the rules move it as a state-based action AFTER the event. The leave is now marked `orphaned` (gameState.detachPermanentFromAll), and a departed watcher never sees it unless the event moved the Aura itself (Akroma's Vengeance destroys Pacifism too — Wicked Visitor drains for it, either order; Evacuation bounces Wicked Visitor and the Pacified Bears — no drain, either order). A battlefield watcher sees it as before (Unsummon on the Bears — Wicked Visitor drains 1).
> · **Marionette Master / Disciple of the Vault / Quill-Slinger Boggart** (life.js): "target (player|opponent) loses life equal to this creature's power" → lose-life with the `sourcePower` count (live; the power it last had when it left — the existing look-backs, plus a new one: a leave event of a permanent whose text says "this creature's power" carries its `sourceLki` record, and a departed watcher's trigger gets it as `abilitySourceLki`); "have target (player|opponent) lose N life" — the causative once the optional wrapper peels "you may" (the triggering-controller causative's twin). Witnessed: the Master (4/6) staying while Shatterstorm takes a Servo → 4; the Master (3/5) and an Ornithopter destroyed together → 3, either order; the Master killed while its trigger waits → its last power (2); an opponent's artifact → nothing. Disciple: your Sol Ring and their Ornithopter → 2; destroyed with an Ornithopter → 1, either order; dying alone → 0. Boggart: a Kithkin spell → the opponent loses 1; Savannah Lions → nothing. Fabricate 3 was already read (Marionette Apprentice's reader). The Master's negative-power ruling is countForSpec's floor at 0.

> · **The bug** (the value-creature entry's found-not-fixed (2) and (3), re-proved on 6cc20920 through the real offers). `pickAttackPlan`
>   filtered a goaded creature's options by the goader's seat id (`!goaders.has(o.defenderId)`), which keeps a non-goader's planeswalker,
>   and `chooseWalkerToKill` then took it: ai1's Bears wearing the user's Shiny Impetus attacked ai2's Jace (Kardur's rule the same);
>   goaded by every opponent, the filter fell back to every option and the walker kill took Jace again. The requirements lived only in the
>   planner, so the offer gave a person's goaded creature every target (the goader, a planeswalker), the play API accepted the attack at
>   the goader, intermediate difficulty's automatic attack took the first target (the goader), and the declaration could close with a
>   Bloodrock Cyclops or a goaded creature at home. Under Silent Arbiter the planner declared its listed-first creature, the cap closed the
>   declaration, and a must-attack creature never attacked (the A/B's game 62). And the planner forced a must-attack creature whose only
>   attacks were taxed: its controller paid Propaganda's {2} to send a 3/3 into a 6/4.
> · **The rules** (bundled CR and rulings, cited exactly). CR 508.1d — a declaration obeying fewer requirements than the maximum possible
>   without disobeying a restriction is illegal; a player is not required to pay a cost to obey one. Goad is CR 701.15 in the bundled rules
>   (the brief's 701.38b names no goad rule): 701.15b — "attacks each combat if able and attacks a player other than the controller of the
>   permanent, spell, or ability that caused it to be goaded if able"; 701.15c — several goaders, additional requirements; 701.15d — the
>   same player again, none. The goad rulings (Shiny Impetus, Disrupt Decorum, Agitator Ant, 2023-06-30): it must attack a player other
>   than the goader if able, else "a planeswalker an opponent controls, a battle an opponent controls, or a player who goaded it"; goaded
>   by each opponent, "the creature must attack an opponent (rather than a planeswalker or battle)"; a cost to attack a player is never
>   forced. Kardur's ruling (2021-02-05) is the same shape ("it must attack you or an opposing planeswalker").
> · **The fix** — `attackRequirements.js` (new leaf over layers, combatEvasion, attackTax, gameState), the one check: `obeyingAttackOptions`
>   (a creature's defenders narrowed to the ones obeying the most "other than X" requirements among the free options — a planeswalker obeys
>   none; a taxed option never raises the bar, stays offered when it ties), `requiredAttackerIds` (a live "attacks each combat if able" —
>   printed less its unless, the layer-6 grant, a forced-attack turn — and a free offered attack), `attackDeclarationOffer` (under an attack
>   cap with no more slots than owed creatures, only those). `layers.attackOtherThanRequirementsOf` counts the requirements (one per goader,
>   one per `requirementOnly` effect); `goaderControllersOf` reads the same grants, unchanged. legalChoices: every attacker's targets go
>   through `obeyingAttackOptions`, and while `required` is non-empty `legalActionsForPlayer` offers only attacker declarations (the pass,
>   a spell, an ability or a mana tap would each close the declaration). opponentAI: the forced set is `requiredAttackerIds`, the per-creature
>   pools are `obeyingAttackOptions` (a no-op on an offered set), the walker kill counts only creatures that may attack a planeswalker;
>   `selfMustAttack` moved to the leaf (re-exported). ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.8 names the module.
> · **Reach** (bundled Commander-legal cards by printed text): goad 82 (17 played natively — Shiny / Coercive / Parasitic Impetus, Jeering
>   Homunculus, Taunting Kobold, Alela, Cunning Conqueror, Redemption Arc, Fast Forward, Coronation of Chaos, Taunting Sliver …), Kardur's
>   rule 1, a self or granted "attacks each combat if able" 99 (53 native), a forced-attack turn 10, an attack cap 3 (Silent Arbiter,
>   Dueling Grounds, Caverns of Despair). Profile decks: Slivers (Bident of Thassa), Veyran Cantrips (Dragon's Rage
>   Channeler), Hulk Smash (Hulk, Brutal Brawler; Hulk, Always Angry), Thrun Voltron (Toski), Halfshell heroes (Fast Forward); caps in
>   Light-Paws Voltron, Nekusar Wheels, Atraxa Superfriends; taxes in Nekusar Wheels and Atraxa Superfriends.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **A "can't attack you" tax is charged on attacks at that player's planeswalkers** — `attackTaxDetail` /
>   `attackTaxToDeclare` (attackTax.js:116, :96) are keyed on the defending player, so Propaganda, Ghostly Prison and Windborn Muse price an
>   attack on their controller's planeswalker as well (legalChoices `canPayAttackTax`, actionDispatcher `applyDeclareAttacker`'s payment);
>   only the "you or planeswalkers you control" printing (Baird, Archon of Absolution, Sphere of Safety) reaches one. The planeswalker
>   attack is withheld when the tax is unaffordable (FN) or charged when it should be free. (2) Per-defender attack caps (Crawlspace) are
>   not modelled (staticAbilityParser.js:3235); if one is, the module's creature-by-creature narrowing (each creature's defender choice
>   independent of the others') no longer holds and needs a joint check. (3) Safe misses, documented in the module: a must-attack creature
>   that "can't attack alone" isn't offered until a teammate is declared, so it doesn't hold the declaration open; under a cap the required
>   creatures aren't ranked by how many requirements each obeys. (4) `applyDeclareAttacker` doesn't check requirements itself — every play
>   path gates on the offered set (`learnSession.applyChoice` → `resolveChoice`, `gameApi.applyAction`, the decide seam's
>   `actionInOfferedSet`); a direct `dispatchAction` (tests, previews) is unchecked. (5) The attack-tax comments cite CR 508.1g (optional
>   costs to attack); the tax is a cost to attack, CR 508.1h (legalChoices.js:43, attackTax.js:2). (6) Pre-existing turn stall, seen only in
>   the supplement (seed 3724842652; Wolverine, claws out! / Jurassic Ramp / Earth Bent / Believe it!), identical on 6cc20920: Jurassic
>   Ramp's Apex Altisaur, put onto the battlefield by Savage Order, fights the same Earth Bent creature (perm-104) 2,000 times in turn 32 —
>   each fight enrages it again, neither dies, and the AI keeps choosing a target where "up to one target" lets it stop; engine-stuck at
>   20,001 ticks.

The join already existed (Leonin Warleader, Parhelion II: `applyCreateToken` registers the minted tokens in `state.combat.attackers` against `ctx.defenderId`). Missing: the plural "…tokens that are tapped and attacking" with no keyword list was split at its internal " and " (splitClauses' keep-whole now takes both forms), and the singular "…token that's tapped and attacking" was never read on the fixed-count arm (the attacking rider now takes "that's"). Only the attack events supply the defender, so `triggerRouting.atomPutsTokensOntoBattlefieldAttacking` — the atom or one it carries (an optional payment's payoff, a conditional branch, a "does the same" inner) — refuses the disposition on any other event and coverage's spell gate refuses it on a spell: "Whenever you attack" (Gut, True Soul Zealot; Undercellar Sweep; Dark Wings Bring Your Downfall) has no defender in its context and stays parked; the per-opponent form (Endless Foot Assault, Adeline) names its own players and is exempt. "a nontoken creature you control attacks" → `creatureYouControl` + `nontokenFilter` (Mardu Ascendancy, Militia's Pride — a declared token attacker makes no Goblin).
