Dies: the death look-back's power (`ctx.dyingPower` — Elenda's and Nested Shambler's rulings, witnessed with counters and with an anthem); enters / attacks: the live power. The X-where arm reads "create X tapped …" (Nested Shambler; Wickersmith's Tools' Scarecrows from its sacrificed counters). Murder Investigation's "its" (the enchanted creature) is never rewritten — parked.

The sourcePower reader answered 0 for a source gone while its ability waited — Krenko removed in response made no Goblins. `gameState.stampAbilitySourceLki` now also stamps every stack ability whose program reads sourcePower (`programReadsSourcePower`) and every waiting trigger whose effect clause names "this creature's power", with `power` on the record (`abilitySourceRecord`); `countForSpec` reads it for that id only, after the sacrifice-cost and dies look-backs.
> · **"exile target card from a graveyard", mandatory.** Its target intent was "ambiguous" ("it could be forced onto its own side"), parking every such trigger. Since the forced-target pick (2026-10-16) that is the rule — a mandatory trigger takes a legal target (CR 603.3d) — so the single mandatory form reads "enemy" (programQueries): an opponent's card when there is one, else the forced pick's least valuable card of its controller's (witnessed: the Island before the Grizzly Bears, logged `trigger-target-forced`); every graveyard empty, nothing happens. A multi-target mandatory form stays ambiguous.
> · **"If it was a <type> card" / "If a <type> card is (was) exiled this way".** parseEffectClauseImpl collapses the exile and its payoff into one program: the payoff atoms carry `ifExiledCardType`, and runEffectProgram runs them only when that exile moved a card of the type (read in its owner's exile zone, front face — CR 712.8a; "permanent" is CR 110.4a's six). The payoff must be non-targeting, non-optional and non-pausing and the exile non-optional ("you may exile …" stays unread). Scavenging Ooze's ruling witnessed: the target gone at resolution, no counter and no life (CR 608.2b); two activations on one creature card, only the first does anything. > · **The conditional tap augment** (`whenProduces` — staticAbilityParser.parseGlobalTapManaAugment → manaModel.globalTapManaAugment):
>   Forsaken Monument ("Whenever you tap a permanent for {C}, add an additional {C}."), Caged Sun ("Whenever a land's ability causes you to
>   add one or more mana of the chosen color, add an additional one mana of that color.", controller-scoped) and Gauntlet of Power
>   ("Whenever a basic land is tapped for mana of the chosen color, its controller adds an additional one mana of that color.", any player):
>   the extra mana is added only when the tap's own mana includes that colour (Forsaken Monument's rulings: a {T} mana ability only, only if
>   it produces {C}, one additional {C} however many it made). "Chosen" resolves off the carrier's `chosenColor`, only on a card that prints
>   the chooser. manaSources drops the bonus from a record that can't make its colour; planPaymentCore's `tapSource` credits it only when
>   the primary's colour (or a fixed bundle) holds it, and a generic tap's primary prefers a colour that triggers one (Breeding Pool under a
>   green Caged Sun taps {G}{G} for {2}); `manualManaTaps` attaches it per colour; commitManaTap adds exactly the plan's picks. Each new
>   parse arm has its $-anchored line in `stripGlobalTapManaAugment`.
> · **All-players subtype augments** — Vernal Bloom / Gauntlet of Might ("Whenever a Forest / Mountain is tapped for mana, its controller
>   adds an additional {G} / {R}"), whatever the land was tapped for (the Gauntlet of Might ruling: a dual with Mountain among its types makes
>   the extra {R} for either colour); Lavaleaper's basic-land Mana Flare line (`basic-land` + sameAsProduced). A fixed bonus that makes the
>   wanted colour now takes it while the primary pays another still-needed colour (`bonusTakesWant`): one Breeding Pool under Vernal Bloom
>   or Utopia Sprawl pays {U}{G} (it had refused under Vernal Bloom — a false "can't afford").
> · **Until end of turn** — High Tide and Bubbling Muck ("Until end of turn, whenever a player taps an Island / a Swamp for mana, that player
>   adds an additional {U} / {B}.") and Molten Tide's "you" form: the `tap-mana-augment-eot` atom (effects/atoms/misc.js) records
>   `{ controller, subject, allPlayers, colors, amount, turn }` in `state.tapManaAugmentsEot`; globalTapManaAugment reads only this turn's
>   entries (CR 514.2). Per the rulings, an Island that entered after it resolved counts, and so does any land with the Island type.
> · **Throne of Eldraine** — `choosesColorOnEnter` reads the name-led chooser ("As Throne of Eldraine enters, choose a color."; a legendary
>   card's short name too), so the enter sites stamp it; the chosen-colour mana leg reads "four mana of the chosen color";
>   `parseSpendRestriction` reads "to cast monocolored spells of that color" (`castMonocolored: "@chosenColor"` → resolveSourceRestriction
>   → the permanent's colour; spendRestrictionAllows: `colorsOfSpell` of the cast card is exactly that colour, a hybrid pip counting both).
>   The draw line's "Spend only mana of the chosen color to activate this ability." is peeled by abilities.js (`spendOnlyChosenColor`, only
>   beside a chooser) and actionsActivateAbility turns its {3} into three pips of the colour, so the action's cost is what the dispatcher
>   pays. Coverage admits the chooser sentence (staticAbilitiesCoverCard; the mana tier's `stripChooseColorSentence`).
> · **FIX (false positive): the restricted surplus.** A restricted tap's mana the payment leaves unspent keeps its restriction (CR 106.6):

>   commitPaymentPlan moves it from the open pool into `player.restrictedMana` (the QUARTET Phase 4 entries — drained at each step's end,

> ## 🔧 2026-10-17 — FIX (engine rules): a player leaving a multiplayer game follows CR 800.4a — the control effects giving them control end first (a creature they took with Control Magic, Act of Treason or Sliver Overlord goes to the player beneath; it vanished with them), every object they own leaves the game wherever it is (a creature of theirs another player had stolen, their Aura on another player's creature, a card of theirs another player was casting — all stayed), their abilities, spell copies and waiting triggers cease to exist (CR 800.4d), and what they still control is exiled to its owners' exile (a creature they reanimated from another player's graveyard — it vanished); their Banishing Light returns the card it held (CR 610.3) while an Oblivion Ring's triggered return does not; other players' Equipment and Auras come off their creatures; the monarch passes to the active player (CR 725.4); an extra turn queued for them is skipped (CR 800.4k) · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,531 unchanged
> Suite **20,880 green (1 skipped) / 1,884 files** under the gate queue (with the rules index built for the run, then deleted). Lint 0
> (CR citations: 0 of 11,727 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,383 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0**
> (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of 80b09e9e, snapshotted before the first edit; native+land 15,531 of 34,584 snapshot
> names on both). **Mutants 6/6** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256): `releaseControlOnLeave` keeping the leaver's own
> stashed home (2 tests red), no `defaultController` stamp in `moveControl` (2), only the leaver's own battlefield leaving (2 — the
> stolen Griffin, the stolen Drone token), stack spells judged by controller alone (2), no CR 800.4d gate in `flushTriggers` (1 — the
> logged drop), the two-trigger detain return handed to a seated player too (1 — Oblivion Ring). Witness `playerLeavesGame.test.js`
> written first: the first 18 run on the untouched 80b09e9e archive — **14 fail on assertions, the 4 controls pass**; with the three added
> while building (the stolen Drone token, the leaver's own Drone token, Oblivion Ring), **16 of the final 21 fail on the archive on
> assertions, the 5 controls pass on both**. A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI;
> base = the untouched 80b09e9e archive): **74 / 80 byte-identical**; the other **6 change no decision** (every row's action, the winner,
> result and turn count identical) — 4 log a dropped leaves trigger of the departed player's own permanent (Watcher for Tomorrow, Cryogen
> Relic, Detention Sphere, Skyclave Apparition; base never recorded the leave, and `orderTriggersAPNAP` would have dropped them silently),
> and in 2 a survivor's Aura on the departed player's creature (Swift Reconfiguration and Detainment Spell; Kenrith's Transformation) goes
> to the graveyard as they leave instead of at the next state-based check (one decision row's `own_permanents` feature differs). 0 errors
> on either tree, results unchanged (ai-wins 60 / user-wins 20), 185 s / 179 s. **158 eliminations** on both trees; **in none was a stolen
> or borrowed object involved** — measured on base with a scratch instrumentation at each elimination (80 / 80 games reproduced): no
> permanent the leaver owned on another battlefield, none another player owned on theirs, no control effect giving them control, no
> cross-owner spell on the stack. No profile deck casts a theft card the engine models (the control-timestamp entry's census).
> Committed on `day/leavegame`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The bug.** `learnSession.removePlayerFromGame` deleted the leaving player's record — their whole battlefield with it — and filtered
>   the stack by controller. Reproduced on 80b09e9e through the session's real elimination (advanceUntilDecision): a creature the leaver
>   held with Control Magic, Act of Treason or Sliver Overlord vanished (CR 800.4a's own examples: it reverts); the leaver's creature
>   another player stole with Mind Control stayed, the Aura on it; the leaver's Pacifism left a dangling id in its host's `attachments`
>   (read by Reyav-style "enchanted or equipped" gates); another player's Bonesplitter on the leaver's creature kept `attachedTo` pointing
>   at nothing and their Pacifism on it stayed on the battlefield until a later check; a card of the leaver's that another player was
>   casting (Ragavan's permission) stayed on the stack, and another player's card the leaver was casting vanished; a creature the leaver
>   reanimated from another player's graveyard vanished (owned by that player: CR 800.4a exiles it); the leaver's waiting trigger stayed
>   queued; a card their Banishing Light held stayed exiled for good; the monarch stayed with the departed seat (nobody could take the
>   crown again); an extra turn queued for them began with them as the active player.
> · **The fix** (`playerLeavesGame.js`, new — learnSession imports it). In CR 800.4a's order: ① the control effects giving the leaver
>   control end first, while they are still seated (`controlMove.releaseControlOnLeave`: the latest remaining effect's controller, else
>   `controlOriginal` unless it is the leaver, else the default controller unless it is the leaver; nobody → it stays for ③). The default
>   controller (CR 110.2) is a new stamp, `defaultController`, that `moveControl` writes on a permanent's first move — the seat it left —
>   so a permanent the leaver controls by default (exiled) is told apart from one an effect gave them (released). Then every permanent the
>   leaver owns, on any battlefield, leaves through `gameState.removePermanentFromGame` (the battlefield exit without a landing: the
>   nonland-left stamp, the trigger look-backs, `detachPermanentFromAll` — attachments fall off, a control Aura releases its host, leave
>   events record so leaves-the-battlefield abilities trigger, CR 603.6c), attachments first; each spell they own leaves the stack. ② Their
>   abilities and spell copies on the stack cease to exist; their waiting and delayed triggers go; `flushTriggers` drops (and logs) any
>   later trigger a departed player would control (CR 800.4d). ③ What they still control is exiled to its owners' exile by the ordinary
>   zone move; a spell they are casting that another player owns goes to its owner's exile. Phased-out permanents: theirs leave every
>   list (CR 702.26k), another player's on their list is exiled. Then the seat (turn order, combat, commander damage — now also from a
>   commander of theirs on another battlefield or the stack — the player-Aura sweep, the monarch via `becomeMonarch`, priority to the next
>   seat in turn order, CR 800.4a). The driver re-runs the SBA check after a removal before anyone gets priority (CR 704.3 — the leave
>   triggers reach the queue first); simultaneous leavers go active player last; `advanceStep` skips an extra turn of a departed player
>   (CR 800.4k). A detainer's return (CR 610.3 — a one-shot, not a trigger) whose controller has left goes to the active player
>   (`checkLeavesTriggers`); the two-trigger printing `foldTwoTriggerDetain` rewrites (Oblivion Ring, Journey to Nowhere) returns with a
>   triggered ability, so it keeps its departed controller and is dropped (`triggers.detainReturnIsTriggered`). A `left-game-objects`
>   log entry names what crossed between players (none in a plain elimination).
> · **Reach.** Every 4-player game with an elimination (158 in the 80 A/B games). The cards whose leave behaviour changes: the 14 control
>   Auras and 15 native threatens of the control-timestamp entry, Sliver Overlord, Hellkite Tyrant, Homeward Path (what they took goes
>   back), every reanimation of another player's creature, every Banishing-Light-style "until" detainer (its card returns) and every
>   leaves-the-battlefield watcher a survivor controls. No tier moves (flip-diff 0).
> · **Tests changed on purpose:** none. Comments updated where they named the old location (`adelineResplendentCathar.test.js`,
>   `ownerZoneRouting.test.js` — its stale-owner board is now built by hand; the fallback it pins stays as the never-throw guard).
> · **Judgement calls:** (1) The leaver's own leave triggers and an Oblivion Ring's return are dropped (CR 800.4d) — the A/B shows
>   `orderTriggersAPNAP` already dropped such triggers silently; the gate makes the drop visible. (2) An attack on the leaver is still
>   removed from combat (base behaviour; CR 800.4e only says no damage is assigned to them). (3) Priority the leaver held passes to the
>   next seat (CR 800.4a); the pass count still restarts, so players who had passed are asked again. (4) The Ragavan permission stamp and
>   a pre-attached Bonesplitter are staged; every other steal, cast and elimination goes through the engine's real entry points. (5) The
>   detain return's stack controller, when its own has left, is the active player (CR 610.3c makes the controller irrelevant to where the
>   card goes). (6) Survivor-controlled leaves triggers of the leaver's objects now fire (the stolen Drone token's drain), per CR 603.6c.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) CR 800.4c — a permanent the leaver controlled by default, held by another player's temporary effect when
>   they leave, stays with its holder when that effect ends (`controlMove.endControlEffects`' pinned fallback); the rule exiles it.
>   (2) CR 800.4g — a pending resolution-time choice of the leaver's (`state.pendingDiscover` / `state.pendingChoice`, settled in
>   learnSession.advanceUntilDecision) is not handed to another player; the settlers assume the seat exists. (3) CR 800.4j — the active
>   player leaving still cuts the turn short (`playerLeavesGame.js` active branch, the B3 simplification). (4) CR 800.4m — the leaver's
>   "until your next turn" effects end at once (`gameState.expireDamageReplacementEffects`). (5) Another player's Aura or Equipment that
>   phased out with a leaver's permanent (a CR 702.26g rider) is lost with the leaver's phased-out list (CR 702.26n). (6) The initiative
>   (CR 726.4) is not modelled.
> · Witness: `playerLeavesGame.test.js` (21 — 16 witnesses, 5 controls).

> · **The policy** — `opponentAI.pickTargetedActivation`, in the ability block after the fetch crack and before the generic picker; own main
>   phase, stack empty (the engine offers non-combat activations there only); the program's one targeted atom read off the parse, its other
>   atoms gains only (gain life, each opponent loses life, draw, scry, surveil, a +1/+1 counter on the source — an "Add" holds). Costs: tap

>   attacker while the defender has an untapped creature (the source's tap never costs a bigger attacker); (1.5 / 1) postcombat only, a shot

> · **The bug.** Every control change goes through `controlMove.moveControl`, but the history of WHY a permanent was held was one
>   level deep: `controlOriginal` plus either `controlUntilEndOfTurn: true` (the threaten, 1760fe36) or `controlStolenBy: <Aura>` (the
>   control Auras, 0c19d9c0). The cleanup sweep sent anything flagged straight to `controlOriginal`, the Aura revert likewise, and the
>   indefinite steal and the Aura attach carried the other's flag along untouched. Probed on d94d164b (all through real casts): Act of
>   Treason then Control Magic — at cleanup the creature went home with the Aura still attached (same player or another; the Aura's
>   attach was a no-op for the same player, so the threaten's flag decided); Control Magic then Act of Treason — at cleanup it went to the
>   owner (the sweep sent it to `controlOriginal`, the owner, past the Aura still attached); Act of Treason then Sliver Overlord — the
>   atom skipped an already-controlled target (`from === controller`) or moved it with the flag, and cleanup reverted the permanent
>   steal (the Hellkite Tyrant entry's found-not-fixed (4): effects/atoms/control.js:165); Control Magic, a third player's Act of Treason,
>   the Aura destroyed — the creature went home at once instead of staying with the threatener until cleanup (and the reverse order the
>   same); two control Auras — removing the later sent the host home past the earlier (pinned in controlAura.test.js as a known
>   simplification since 2026-07-29); **Illusory Gains** ("Whenever a creature an opponent controls enters, attach this Aura to that
>   creature.", native-trigger) and a control Aura moved by Codsworth — `attachPermanent` detached the Aura from its old host
>   without ending its effect, so the first creature stayed stolen for good and the second was stolen too.
> · **The fix (CR 613.1b, 613.7).** controlMove.js owns a control-effect record per permanent: `controlEffects` — the temporary effects
>   on it, oldest first, `{to, until: "end-of-turn"}` (a threaten, ends in the cleanup step, CR 514.2) or `{to, aura}` (a control Aura,
>   ends when it stops being attached; a re-attach is a new timestamp, CR 613.7e) — over `controlOriginal` (who controls it once they
>   have all ended). Three writers, nothing else touches the fields: `addControlEffect` (a threaten, an Aura attaching — its player
>   controls it now; not recorded when nothing beneath it can end and its player already has it), `endControlEffects` (the cleanup sweep,
>   an Aura leaving through the battlefield-exit chokepoint, an Aura moved off by `attachPermanent` — the permanent goes to the latest
>   remaining effect's controller, else home; a player who has left is skipped, CR 800.4a; if none is left it stays), and
>   `gainControlIndefinitely` (Sliver Overlord, Hellkite Tyrant, Homeward Path / Trostani Discordant — no duration, CR 611.2a, later
>   than everything on the permanent, so the record is cleared). The single-target atom no longer skips a target it already controls
>   when a temporary effect holds it, and Homeward Path also takes a creature its owner holds only through a temporary effect (an owner
>   who threatened it back from a Control Magic keeps it past cleanup — the base got this right by accident, and the record would
>   otherwise have handed it to the Aura's controller). A pre-record save's `controlUntilEndOfTurn` / `controlStolenBy` is read as the
>   equivalent list (pinned). `playability-sweep.mjs` counts Aura entries instead of `controlStolenBy`.
> · **Reach.** The bundled cards whose modelled control change now behaves differently in these interactions — 34 native: the 15
>   native threatens (Act of Treason, Traitorous Blood, Turn Against, Portent of Betrayal, Vengeful Possession, Pack's Betrayal, Lose
>   Calm, Involuntary Employment, Song-Mad Treachery, Limits of Solidarity, Bloody Betrayal, Twisted Fealty, Press into Service,
>   Tentative Connection, Sarkhan Vol), the 14 control Auras (Control Magic, Mind Control, Treachery, Persuasion, Corrupted Conscience,
>   Mind Harness, Threads of Disloyalty, Yavimaya's Embrace, Spirit Away, Biting Tether, Binding Grasp, Vapor Snare, Mark of the Oni,
>   Illusory Gains) and Hypnotic Siren (bestowed), Sliver Overlord, Hellkite Tyrant (no visible change: its clear already made a later
>   Aura revert a no-op), Homeward Path and Trostani Discordant; plus Codsworth, Handy Helper as the mover. No tier moves (flip-diff 0).
>   Profile decks: The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl holds Homeward Path; Captain America and Light-Paws hold Codsworth but no control Aura;
>   Bumble Flower Combo holds Eriette's Tempting Apple, whose steal is unmodelled (body-only). No theft deck is added (the 08-15 veto).
> · **Tests changed on purpose:** `controlAura.test.js`'s "⚠️ KNOWN SIMPLIFICATION" pin (two Auras → home) now asserts the CR answer (the
>   first Aura's controller, then home when it goes too) — fails on the archive; `threatenControl.test.js`'s stamp assertion reads
>   `controlEffects` instead of `controlUntilEndOfTurn`.
> · **Judgement calls:** (1) Act of Treason stands in for "Threaten" — Threaten's own text ("Untap target creature and gain control of it
>   until end of turn") is not read (arbiter-spell), Act of Treason is the native member. (2) The indefinite single-target steal is

> · **The bug** (found in the graveyard-exile slice; measured on ee70e7d9). The planner skipped `cost.phyrexian` ("assumed paid with
>   life") and no cast or activation charged the life: Dismember off one Island cost the Island and nothing else, Gitaxian Probe was free,
>   Immolating Souleater pumped for nothing, Lashwrithe equipped for nothing. A hybrid Phyrexian symbol ({G/U/P}) was parsed as plain
>   hybrid — payable with mana only. Only the attack tax's Norn's Annex lane charged the life, in its own copy.
> · **Reach** (every bundled card, the mana cost and every activated cost read): **74 cards** hold a Phyrexian symbol — 38 in a mana cost
>   (4 of them hybrid Phyrexian: the compleated walkers Ajani, Sleeper Agent; Lukka, Bound to Ruin; Nahiri, the Unforgiving; Tamiyo,
>   Compleated Sage), 39 in an activated cost (35 only there — the transform DFCs, the Souleaters, the Dominuses, Spellskite, Hex
>   Parasite …), 4 in both (Birthing Pod, Moltensteel Dragon, Spike, Synthesis Pod), and Lashwrithe's Equip {B/P}{B/P}. **29 are credited
>   native**: casts — Corrosive Gale, Dismember, Gitaxian Probe, Gut Shot, Marrow Shards, Mental Misstep, Mutagenic Growth, Norn's Annex,
>   Noxious Revival, Phyrexian Metamorph, Pith Driller, Porcelain Legionnaire, Slash Panther, Spined Thopter, Tezzeret's Gambit, Thundering
>   Tanadon, Vault Skirge; cast + ability — Birthing Pod, Moltensteel Dragon; ability — Blinding, Immolating, Insatiable, Pestilent and
>   Trespassing Souleater, Drivnod, Mondrak, Solphim, Zopandrel; Lashwrithe's equip. **Every one now pays faithfully** — swept on a board
>   whose Wastes pay only the generic part, at 20 life: each was offered, stamped, and took 2 life per symbol (base: 0 life for all 30
>   offers); Mental Misstep checked on the stack against a Lightning Bolt (2 life). The 7 compleated walkers are arbiter-pw (their cost is
>   paid; they don't resolve yet). Profile decks: Mondrak (Vihaan), Skrelv, Defector Mite (Shalai and Hallar — body-only), Solphim
>   (Nekusar), Zopandrel (Thrun), Dismember (Believe it!), Gitaxian Probe (Veyran), Mental Misstep (cdh, Believe it!, Kinnan), Norn's Annex
>   (Atraxa), Noxious Revival (Killer Turts, Squirrel Girl, Test Rashmi), Phyrexian Metamorph (cdh, Kinnan).
> · **The fix** (manaModel). `planWithPhyrexian` wraps planPayment and canAfford: the fewest symbols in life first (none, one, two … —
>   each set of that size in symbol order), every other symbol turned into its coloured pip (a hybrid one into a hybrid pip), so mana pays
>   whenever it can; the life is a base claim of the payment (consumedClaimsPayable — beside a Mana Confluence's life, at least 1 left; the
>   claims ride the passes into the core and the costed path); it needs the payer's life in the spend context (`lifePaymentContext` —
>   `life`, `lifeLocked`), and with none a symbol needs its mana (never free). The plan's `phyrexianLife` is charged by commitPaymentPlan
>   (loseLife, a `phyrexian-life` log line). payManaCost passes the life and no longer reads a lone {W/P} as an empty cost. parseManaCost
>   keeps a hybrid Phyrexian symbol as one Phyrexian entry ("G/U").
> · **The paths.** The dispatcher's cast and activation (Equip included) pass the payer's life; the attack tax pays Norn's Annex through
>   payManaCost — the second copy (all-mana, else all-life) is gone, and legalChoices withholds on the same planner. The offer's cast and
>   activation contexts carry the life (X spells too); the new last pass `withPhyrexianPayment` prices each Phyrexian cast/activation with
>   the payment's own plan (`offeredPaymentPlan`, shared with withPayableConsumedCosts), drops the unpayable and stamps `phyrexianLife`;
>   the label names it ("pay 4 life for its Phyrexian mana"); opponentAI.pickAction drops a stamped action that would leave it below
>   LIFE_PRUDENCE_FLOOR (10) — held, as the coordinator's policy asks: mana when it has the colour, life above the floor, else hold.
> · **Graduated:** `nornsAnnex.test.js` "no white source at 1 life: withheld; at exactly 2 life: offered, and the attacker goes to 0" →
>   "at 1 or 2 life withheld; at 3 offered, the attacker goes to 1": the Annex pip now follows the engine's policy for every life payment
>   (paying to exactly 0 is legal, CR 119.4, and loses the game).
> · **Mutants (11/11 on assertions):** the planner skipping the symbols; no life lane; the commit not charging; the life no claim of the
>   payment; the life lock ignored; life paid down to 0; hybrid Phyrexian read as hybrid; the AI paying below the floor; a lone pip read
>   as an empty cost (killed by the Norn's Annex tests); no stamp; life tried before mana.
> · **⚑ Judgment calls.** (1) Mana first, fewest life — the engine never pays life a board could pay in mana; a person who wants to keep a
>   land up can't choose life instead (auto-payment only). (2) The policy keeps 1 life per payment, Phyrexian life included: Dismember
>   off an Island at 4 life is not offered (legal per CR 119.4, but it loses the game). (3) The AI's floor (10) is its existing life floor;
>   at 11 life it holds Vault Skirge off an Island. (4) Compleated (CR 702.150a: two fewer loyalty counters per symbol paid with life) is
>   not modeled — those walkers don't resolve today, so paying their cost with life grants nothing; it must come with their resolution.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) Compleated, above (7 planeswalkers). (2) The other cost sites without the payer's life — cycling,
>   "discard this card" abilities, plot, suspend, turn face up, companion, the hand self-put — pay a Phyrexian symbol with mana only (none
>   in the bundle prints one there today). (3) Cast variants priced without the caster's life (kicker, bestow, emerge, the sacrifice-cost
>   cast lanes) need the symbol's mana — a false negative where a Phyrexian card has such a variant.

>   "untapped" when no land's mana casts anything this turn — that is what "an untapped dual over a tapped-delivery fetch when it needs to
>   cast this turn; the fetch when it finds a colour it lacks and the dual doesn't" asks, and it applies to every land, not only fetches
>   (the comparison is fair only if it is one rule): the 56 ordinary-land flips are 29 untapped → tapped (a land of a colour already made,
>   or one that makes nothing now — Glacial Chasm, Temple of the False God — giving way to a tapland of the missing colour) and 27 untapped →
>   untapped (Gaea's Cradle with no creatures, a summoning-sick Dryad Arbor, Dark Depths, Serra's Sanctum, Arena giving way to a land whose
>   mana casts now or fills the gap). With nothing to cast and no gap, untapped still goes first (the old tie order — see found-not-fixed).
>   ~71 ms of a 16 s two-game profile is the land drop.
> · **Part 2 — every land search** (`fetchLand.landSearchPickOrder`, replacing the fetch-only `isFetchLandSearch` gate). A tutor-search from
>   the library (Demonic Consultation's name pick is not one) whose every filter alternative names a land ("basic land", "Forest", "Plains,
>   Island, Swamp, or Mountain", "snow land", "land"), to the battlefield, hand or top — not the graveyard — takes `landSearchOrder`: the
>   unmet pips of the hand and command zone in the colours it makes, then all their pips, then the old order. Each pick is read afresh, so
>   Cultivate / Kodama's Reach put the most-needed colour onto the battlefield and the next need into the hand. Kept on the old order: any
>   non-land alternative ("a creature or land card" — Archdruid's Charm, Moonsilver Key), "a card", a graveyard destination, a land put
>   from the hand (Growth Spiral, Uro — the same choice kind, no search).
> · **Tests changed on purpose:** `fetchLandCrack.test.js`'s control "Rampant Growth takes the Forest" is now the witness "takes the Swamp";
>   `sncFetchLands.test.js`'s control "the Overlook over Dimir Guildgate (it is not ranked as the tapped land it becomes)" is now the witness
>   "Dimir Guildgate over the Overlook", and its land-drop fixture's library gained a Swamp (the family land's colours are now the
>   library's — with only a Forest, Maestros Theater finds nothing).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) The land-search score weighs colours only: it takes a land that enters tapped over one that doesn't
>   (Nature's Lore: Breeding Pool → Spara's Headquarters; Three Visits → Ketria / Indatha Triome; the fetch's Marsh Flats → Savai Triome),
>   and a colour land over a utility one with every colour already made (Sowing Mycospawn / Crop Rotation: Ancient Tomb → Forest, City of
>   Brass) — fetchLand.js:155 `colourScore`. (2) `landEntersTapped` (opponentAI.js:236) reads shocklands and check lands
>   ("… enters tapped unless …", "If you don't, it enters tapped") as tapped, though the AI's shock policy pays 2 life above 12: such a land
>   never "casts now", and a fetch whose best find is a shock reads tapped (Misty Rainforest → Breeding Pool, both read tapped, decided by
>   name). (3) With nothing to cast this turn and no colour gap, an untapped land still goes ahead of a tapland — the tapland should go
>   first then (the untapped one keeps for a turn that needs it); the old tie order, left for its own slice. (4) "Casts now" checks one card
>   at a time at its printed cost (no reductions, alternative costs, or a second spell the extra mana would add). (5) A land put from the
>   hand (Growth Spiral, Uro, Arboreal Grazer) keeps highest mana value, then name.
> · Witness: `fetchLandDrop.test.js` (27 — 17 witnesses, 10 controls). Updated: `fetchLandCrack.test.js` (25), `sncFetchLands.test.js` (16).

> · **The bug** (found by the opponent-scoped damage slice; reproduced). The {X} lane in `legalChoices.actionsActivateAbility` built its
>   own actions above the shared enumeration and carried only the costs it knew (life, energy, the self-sacrifice / self-exile / counter
>   items, the two discards): "Sacrifice another creature" and "Sacrifice a Clue" rode as `sacCreatureId: null`, and the dispatcher pays
>   only what the action names. Measured on the base engine: Fiend Artisan beside three Swamps and no other creature offered X = 1 and X = 2;
>   with two other creatures it offered one action per X and none named a victim; Phyrexian Altar + the only other creature + one Swamp
>   offered X = 1 (the Altar counted, its only food the Artisan's own victim); Alquist Proft with no Clue offered X = 1. The tap-others,
>   counted-sacrifice, return-a-land and unattach costs were dropped the same way (probe texts — no bundled card carries one beside a
>   modeled {X}), and the exile-from-graveyard cost refused the whole ability. The lane also expanded its targets without the source, so a
>   creature's {X} ability could target a creature with protection from creatures (the printed-cost lane already passed it).
> · **The fix** (legalChoices only; the dispatcher already paid every field). The X choice is one more dimension of the shared lane: the
>   victim pools (sacOther, sacCount, tapCreature, returnLand, unattachEquipment, exileGyCount, the discards) are gathered for an {X}
>   ability as for any other; each per-victim affordability check is a function of the cost it judges — the printed cost, or X = 1
>   (`gateCost`) above the walk, then every X from 1 up to the pool-plus-sources ceiling (X_CHOICE_CAP) per victim set, stopping at the first
>   X that set can't pay (monotonic); the targets are expanded once per X with `{ sourceId, xValue }` (the Candelabra ordering kept) and
>   shared by every victim; one push builds every activation, `xValue` and the "X=N: " text prefix only on the {X} lane. A victim the effect
>   targets is skipped as on the printed-cost lane. Refused, FN-safe, no bundled carrier: an {X} cost with a "Sacrifice X <subtype>" cost
>   (two X choices), and exile-from-graveyard with "Sacrifice X" (the γ1e lane still builds its own action). The victim policy is the
>   printed-cost lane's: one action per legal victim (the player's pick); each victim is its own (an Altar never eats it — the 151790b4
>   reserved set — and a one-shot mana victim such as an Eldrazi Spawn is never also cracked); a repeatable mana creature may tap for mana
>   and then be the victim (Llanowar Elves pays X = 1 and is sacrificed).

> ## 🔧 2026-10-17 — FIX (AI decision quality): the AI cracks its fetch lands — Evolving Wilds, Terramorphic Expanse, Fabled Passage, Prismatic Vista, Escape Tunnel, Vibrant Cityscape and the ten Zendikar / Onslaught fetches were never activated (the generic activation picker skips every sacrifice-self cost), so 24 of the 30 profile decks played a dead land each time they drew one; and a fetch's search now takes the land that makes the colour the hand and commander need most, not the alphabetically first · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,518 unchanged
> Suite **20,650 green (1 skipped) / 1,873 files** under the gate queue (with the rules index built for the run, then deleted). Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of
> 11,457 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,375 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0** (34,620 cards; before = an
> untouched `git archive` of 33e3c9c6, snapshotted before the first edit; native+land 15,518 of 34,584 snapshot names on both). **Mutants 6/6**
> on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256): no crack before the casts, the life floor dropped, the library check dropped, no
> colour pick, a mana cost admitted, unmet colours not weighted first; the first build's "mana cost admitted" survived (the Terminal Moraine
> control had an empty hand, so the Landscape rule never asked) — a control with a colour the hand lacks closes it. Witness
> `fetchLandCrack.test.js` written first: 12 of the first 23 seen to fail on the base engine on assertions (the 11 controls pass on both);
> with the two tests added while building, 13 of the final 25 fail on the untouched 33e3c9c6 archive on assertions, the 12 controls pass on
> both. A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 33e3c9c6 archive):
> fetch activations **0 → 207** (172 life paid; every search found a land), **11 byte-identical, 69 change picks — every first divergence is a
> fetch crack**, 29 winners change, turn counts move in 57, 0 errors on either tree (80 / 80 completed), results ai-wins 57 → 54 / user-wins
> 23 → 26 (an outcome, not the grade); 180 s / 331 s per batch (the after batch ran beside the lint; an identical instrumented rerun took
> 196 s). Committed on `day/fetchcrack`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The cause (probed on 33e3c9c6).** `pickSafeAbilityActivation` (opponentAI.js:1582 at the base) skips every activation with `sacSelf`
>   or a life cost, and nothing else in `pickAction` took a fetch: with Evolving Wilds and a basic in the library the AI passed. At scale, the
>   base batch: 0 fetch activations in 80 games while the AI played 207 fetch lands as land drops (the land drop reads one as an untapped land).
> · **The timing the engine allows.** Every activated ability is offered on its controller's own main phase only (legalChoices.js
>   `actionsActivateAbility`, `mainWindow`; the combat and stack windows admit only combat-role and stack-copy abilities), so there is no
>   opponent's-end-step crack to choose: the AI cracks in its own main phase.
> · **The policy** — `fetchLand.js` (new, a leaf over the parser, the tutor filter and manaModel) + `opponentAI.pickFetchCrack`. A fetch land
>   is an offered activation of a land on the battlefield that taps and sacrifices it, costs no mana and nothing but life, targets nothing,
>   and runs exactly one search for ONE card to the battlefield whose every filter group names a land (`fetchCrackAtom` over the action,
>   `fetchLandAbility` over the card — the parsed ability, never the text). Corpus: 32 lands (the Zendikar / Onslaught ten and Prismatic
>   Vista, the five Mirage fetches, the ten MH3 Landscapes, Evolving Wilds, Terramorphic Expanse, Fabled Passage, Escape Tunnel, Hobbit
>   Hole, Vibrant Cityscape); every other sacrifice-self ability stays skipped (Sakura-Tribe Elder, Mind Stone, the Panoramas, Terminal
>   Moraine — pinned). Cracked only in the AI's own main phase with the stack empty; only while the library holds a land the search finds
>   (the search's own `cardMatchesTutorFilter`); and a life cost only when it leaves the AI at `LIFE_PRUDENCE_FLOOR` (10) or more — the floor
>   Castle Locthwain's loss and the alternative-cost life payments use (life 11 pays, life 10 holds). A fetch land that makes no mana of its
>   own is cracked right after the land drop and BEFORE the casts (an untapped fetched land pays for this turn's spells; a tapped one costs
>   nothing to fetch now); one that taps for mana (the Landscapes' "{T}: Add {C}.") only from the ability block, after the casts, while it
>   is untapped, and only when it finds a colour the hand needs and no battlefield source makes. Deterministic: untapped delivery first, then
>   name, then id. The policy key `fetch` ("v1" = the old hold) joins POLICY_KEYS.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-17 — FIX (false positive): a reflexive trigger chooses its targets when IT goes on the stack (CR 603.12, 603.3d) — Smoke Bomb (EDHREC #4790, credited native, never did anything: its own "All creatures have shroud" met the follow-up's target at the parent's flush, so the upkeep trigger was removed and the artifact never sacrificed) now sacrifices itself and makes a creature unblockable; Primal Witchstalker and Yathan Roadwatcher mill even with nothing to return and can return what they milled; Dream Eater surveils with no opposing nonland permanent; Faebloom Trick is cast with no opposing creature; Red Hulk's and The Royal Scions' damage become abilities of their own · **±0** · snapshot native 15,518 unchanged
> Suite **20,649 green (1 skipped) / 1,873 files** under the gate queue (with the rules index built for the run and deleted after). Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of 11,475 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,374 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff
> **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0** (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of 33e3c9c6, snapshotted before the first edit; native+land
> 15,518 of 34,584 snapshot names on both — no tier moved). `program-fingerprint`: 7 cards' parses move, each by the one new
> `reflexiveTrigger` stamp — Smoke Bomb, Primal Witchstalker, Yathan Roadwatcher, Dream Eater, Faebloom Trick, Red Hulk, and The Last
> Ronin's chapter II (body-only; chapter III unread); the loyalty parse, outside the fingerprint, moves The Royal Scions' −8 and Ajani,
> Nacatl Avenger's 0 (body-only) the same way. **Mutants 8/8** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256). Witness
> `reflexiveTriggerTargets.test.js` written first: **13 of its 24 tests fail on the untouched 33e3c9c6 archive on assertions**, the 11
> controls pass on both. A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the
> untouched 33e3c9c6 archive): **80 / 80 byte-identical** (every decision row, log hash, winner and turn count), 0 errors on either tree,
> results unchanged (ai-wins 57 / user-wins 23) — expected: of the changed cards only Red Hulk sits in a profile deck (Hulk Smash, seated
> in games 40–49), and no game's log names it. The harness sees the engine (hollow-gate check): the same batch with one basic swapped for
> Smoke Bomb in 27 decks — base: cast 46 times, its trigger removed 134 times, never sacrificed, no creature made unblockable; after: 32
> sacrifices by its trigger, 24 creatures made unblockable, 8 reflexives removed for want of a creature; 49 games byte-identical, 31 change
> picks (most first diverge at a priority pass where base took an action — read as the reflexive's own stack window, not traced
> game by game), 7 winners change, 0 errors on either tree. Committed on
> `day/reflextgt`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The bug** (found in the SNC fetch-land slice, reproduced on 33e3c9c6). `parser.matchReflexiveTrigger` folds "<primary>. When you do,
>   <reflexive>." into ONE program, so a targeted reflexive atom was enumerated with the parent's targets — at the parent's flush (or cast,
>   or activation), before the primary's action. A reflexive triggered ability triggers during the resolution, when the action happens
>   (CR 603.12), and is put on the stack the next time a player would receive priority, its targets chosen then (CR 603.3d → 601.2c); the
>   bundled rulings for Smoke Bomb, Yathan Roadwatcher, Faebloom Trick, Dream Eater and Awaken the Honored Dead say so in as many words.
>   Smoke Bomb: no creature can be targeted while it is on the battlefield, so its upkeep trigger was removed (`trigger-removed-no-target`)
>   every turn and it was never sacrificed. Primal Witchstalker / Yathan Roadwatcher: with no land / creature card in the graveyard before
>   the mill, the whole enters trigger was removed — no mill, no return — and a milled card could never be the target. Dream Eater: no
>   opponent nonland permanent → no surveil. Faebloom Trick: not castable without an opposing creature (the spell itself has no target).
> · **The fix — one mechanism, four seams.** (1) `matchReflexiveTrigger` stamps `reflexiveTrigger` on the reflexive's atoms when the
>   reflexive names a chosen target (`programNeedsChosenTarget`) the trigger chooser can place on a side (`programTriggerTargetsResolvable`).
>   (2) `targeting.expandAtoms` skips a stamped atom (keeping its index, as for kicked-only atoms) — so the parent offers / locks no target
>   for it at cast, activation or flush. (3) `runEffectProgram`, reaching the stamped run with its gate open (the `ifSacrificed` gate the
>   SNC slice put on a self-sacrifice primary is checked first), hands the run to `enqueueReflexiveTrigger`: a pending trigger carrying its
>   own program (the atoms, gates spent — it exists only because the action happened), the parent's controller and source (CR 603.7d,
>   603.7e — the spell for a spell, the permanent for an ability) and context, less the parent's per-ability resolution key. (4)
>   `gameEngine.buildTriggerStack` puts it on the stack at the next flush (`buildReflexiveTriggerStack`): the same `expandCastChoices` and
>   `chooseTriggerTargets` every targeted trigger uses, on the board after the action; no legal target → removed and logged. The parent
>   still sees the reflexive's atoms everywhere else (routing, tier, the α1 gate on the whole program), so no tier moves.
> · **Reach** (corpus scan, every bundled card; text from oracle_cards.json). 236 cards print a "When you do" sentence naming a target, 34
>   credited native. Behaviour changes for the 7 natives above (the five fixes; Red Hulk's damage and The Royal Scions' −8 damage now wait
>   on the stack after the counter / the draw — same amount, same chooser, a priority window between). Untouched by design: the 13
>   optional-primary natives (Fireblade Artist, Cornered Crook, Shrapnel Slinger, Selfcraft Mechan, General Traag, Unscrupulous Contractor,
>   Tether Technician, Inti, Kappa Tech-Wrecker, Forgehammer Centurion, Sutina, Awaken the Honored Dead, Generous Plunderer) —
>   below; Undead Butler and Paramecia Coloniex (the optional-exile-self payment wrapper: target at the flush with the
>   exiled card excluded — the same pool the rule gives); Ancient Bronze Dragon (the roll fold upstream; the roll can't change what is
>   legal); Earth Rumble (its fight pair is "ambiguous" to the chooser, so it keeps the cast-time pick it had rather than become a trigger
>   the flush would hand to the Arbiter); the ten conspire / casualty spells (their "When you do, copy …" is the keyword's, read elsewhere).
> · **Judgment calls.** (a) The optional-primary fold ("You may <cost>. When you do, <targeted payoff>", `matchOptionalReflexiveTrigger`)
>   keeps its flush-time target: the AI's optional-effect autopilot always takes the "may" (learnSession's `optionalAutoTakeValue`
>   fallback), so with the target moved after the action it would sacrifice / discard / bounce into a payoff with no legal target —
>   today's flush removes that trigger before the question is asked. Splitting it needs a take/decline read of the payoff's targets first.
>   (b) A human seat no longer picks the target of Faebloom Trick's tap or The Royal Scions' −8 damage at cast / activation: the reflexive
>   is a trigger, and the engine has no interactive trigger-target choice for any seat — `chooseTriggerTargets` picks (enemy-side here),
>   as it does for every other trigger. (c) A source-scoped trigger multiplier (Annie Joins Up, Katara, Cloud) now sees the reflexive as a
>   triggered ability of its source (CR 603.7e) and can multiply it; folded inline it never could. No ruling in the bundled data settles
>   it either way.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) the optional-primary reflexives above — Awaken the Honored Dead's chapter III can't return the card it
>   discards (the bundled ruling says it may) and is removed outright when the graveyard holds no creature or land card
>   (parser.js `matchOptionalReflexiveTrigger`, ~line 2172; the autopilot at learnSession.js:1884). (2) The scaled-damage arms take any
>   source phrase (`atoms/stack.js:532` "^.+? deals? damage to (.+?) equal to the number of", `:551` the modern word order), so a
>   conditional lead is swallowed: Ajani, Nacatl Avenger's 0 ("When you do, if you control a red permanent other than Ajani, he deals
>   damage …") parses HIGH with the "if" dropped. The card is body-only; whether the engine offers that loyalty line was not established.
>   (3) Earth Rumble: the earthbent land can't be the fighter, and the spell can't be cast without an opposing creature (cast-time fight
>   targets — the α1 gap above).
> · Witness: `reflexiveTriggerTargets.test.js` (24). Revised: `reflexiveTrigger.test.js` (the fold's target-opponent payoff carries the

>   set of partial regexes, and two of them read sentences wider than printed: "If a source you control would deal damage[^.]*deals double"

>   <recipient>], <result>." and the "Double all damage <who> would deal." family, off the face that is up (a Class at its level, no leveler band,
>   no Room door — Torture Pit's door state isn't read), a label stripped only when it has no rules meaning (the shared CR 207.2c list, plus

>   creature / planeswalker / battle an opponent controls), "you or a permanent you control", "this creature", "equipped creature"; sources

>   "another creature" (the Flail); "noncombat" (CR 120.2b); results **"that much damage plus N"** (`op: "add"`), "plus X, where X is <self>'s

>   vanguard gain the Hellbent condition), 2 one-shot spells no longer read as a permanent's static (Isengard Unleashed, Insult // Injury — the

>   Goblin made green doesn't). A source off the battlefield: the record the damage event carries (`event.sourceLki`) — a resolving spell's

>   pay {2} (and Grizzly Bears is offered and cast), Phyrexian + Ashnod's Altar + one creature pay {3}, two Gilded Geese + one Food pay {2},
>   two Altars + Gilded Goose + Tough Cookie pay {3} (legal: 2; the commit then threw "Permanent goose not found"), Phyrexian Altar + an
>   Eldrazi Spawn as its only victim pay {2} (the Spawn cracked for itself AND fed to the Altar), Phyrexian Tower's {B}{B} line + Phyrexian
>   Altar + one creature pay {B}{B}{1}, two Altars + one creature fund Simic Signet and still pay {G}{U}{1}, and payGenericMana (the
>   resolution layer) paid {2} off two Altars and one creature. The explicit taps were already right: after one Altar eats the only creature,
>   manaSources offers the other no more (the board is re-read per tap).
> · **The fix** (manaModel). Each sacrifice record carries its eligible victims (`sacVictimIds` — a creature / Food NOW, never the source;
>   main products and extra lines alike; an extra line's `sacrificesFood` now rides its record too). `assignSacVictims` — a distinct victim
>   per cost, depth-first under an augmenting-path bound; a record that leaves as it pays (a self-sacrifice, a depletion land's last counter)
>   takes its permanent out of every list; a source that is another's victim commits first (`sacCommitOrder`: Gilded Goose taps and eats its
>   Food, then Phyrexian Altar eats the Goose — two sources each the other's victim, two Thermopods, have no order). **Planner:**
>   planPaymentCore taps a sacrifice source (or a self-sacrificing one) only while every sacrifice of the payment can still get its own
>   victim (`victimsHold` at the snow, colour and generic picks); activateCostedInOrder's funding, activation and rest calls share one claim
>   list. **Affordability** is the same planner. **Contention retry:** when no plan pays and two sacrifice records share a victim (or a
>   victim sacrifices itself), planPaymentPasses tries once more without each contended record (never nested) — Phyrexian Altar first in
>   board order took the creature, and Ashnod's Altar's {C}{C} from the same creature could no longer pay {2}; a board without contention
>   plans exactly as before. **Commit:** commitPaymentPlan commits every other tap, then assigns the sacrifices on the live board (least
>   valuable first, never `reserved`) and commits them in that order; commitManaTap pays the sacrifice before anything is added, and with no
>   victim it adds, taps and pays nothing (`sacrifice-<kind>-cost-unpaid` logged). The explicit tap keeps its own least-valuable pick.
>   `withoutUnfeedableSacSources` now also narrows each kept source's victims by the reserved permanents.
> · **The action's own cost permanents.** The commit never feeds `reserved` to an Altar, so a planner that counted one left the payment short.
>   Purple Pentapus's "{2}{B}, Tap an untapped creature you control" (graveyard recursion; Otharri the same) was offered, and paid, with
>   Phyrexian Altar eating the very creature the cost taps — phantom mana on base. The offer now checks affordability per tapped creature
>   through withoutUnfeedableSacSources, and applyActivateGyRecursion plans from the same narrowed sources. The emerge offer narrows the Altars'
>   victims by the emerge victim as castPaymentSources already did (base: Wretched Gryff offered off three Islands + an Altar whose only
>   victim was the emerge sacrifice, then MANA_SHORT on dispatch).
> · **Reach** (manaSources over every bundled card with "sacrifice" and "add" — 894 — on a board with two creatures and two Foods): **7 carry a
>   sacrifice-another record** — Phyrexian Altar, Ashnod's Altar, Thermopod, Everythingamajig (main, no {T}), Gilded Goose (a Food), Phyrexian
>   Tower and Lazotep Quarry (extra lines). Profile decks: **none holds two or more**; one holds one beside a Food maker — The Unbeatable
>   Squirrel Girl (Phyrexian Altar; Peregrin Took and The Cabbage Merchant make non-creature Foods, which the Altar can't eat). No profile deck
>   holds Gilded Goose. So the reach in the profile decks is one Phyrexian Altar, whose single-victim payments
>   are unchanged (the assignment's first pick is the old least-valuable pick) unless its only victim sacrifices itself for mana in the same
>   payment or is a permanent the action's own cost claims.
> · **Witness `sacrificeVictimDistinct.test.js`** (25, bundled oracle text): the planner (two Altars + one creature, Phyrexian + Ashnod's with
>   Ashnod's alone still paying {2}, two Geese + one Food, two Altars + Goose + Tough Cookie, Altar + a lone Eldrazi Spawn, Phyrexian Tower's
>   line + Altar, the Signet-funded costed path, a mana bound over {1}–{4}); the commit (no victim → no mana, a planned victim gone → that
>   Altar makes nothing, the Goose pays before the Altar eats it, payGenericMana); runtime (Grizzly Bears not offered off two Altars / two
>   Geese with one victim); the action's own permanents (Purple Pentapus, withoutUnfeedableSacSources' narrowing, emerge); controls (one Altar
>   + one creature; two Altars + two creatures cast Grizzly Bears, each its own victim; two Altars + three creatures take the two least
>   valuable; Goose + Altar + Tough Cookie pay {2}; a Forest is still tapped before the Altar; a creature tapped for mana may still be fed to
>   the Altar afterwards; the explicit taps).
> · **Mutants (9/9 on assertions):** the planner's claim check off; the commit adding the mana with no victim; the costed rest call without the
>   earlier claims; the commit in plan order; no contention retry; withoutUnfeedableSacSources keeping reserved victims; a self-sacrificing
>   source left in the victim lists; the Pentapus offer and the emerge offer un-narrowed. (The first build of the second mutant was itself
>   malformed — a TypeError, not an assertion — and was rewritten before it counted.)
> · **⚑ Judgment calls.** (1) Thermopod may sacrifice itself ("Sacrifice a creature" names no "another"); the engine keeps every sacrifice
>   source's victim another permanent (as SG-3 did), so two Thermopods now pay one {R} where base paid two by an illegal sequence (the second
>   Thermopod activated after it was sacrificed) — a safe false negative, unchanged in kind. (2) The contention retry is one level deep: a board
>   needing two records left out to find its plan stays unpayable (FN-safe). (3) A sacrifice record without `sacVictimIds` (none is built
>   outside manaSources) is planned as having no victim.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **The exile-from-graveyard cost has the same shape** — Molt Tender and Rubble Rouser ("{T}, Exile a card from your
>   graveyard: Add …", the only two bundled carriers): two of them beside one graveyard card pay {2} (measured), since the planner counts no
>   graveyard cards across sources and commitManaTap's exile branch logs `exile-gy-cost-unpaid` and keeps the mana (manaModel.js:4387). (2)
>   The activated-ability offer's fast path (legalChoices.js:2783) doesn't narrow the Altars' victims by the activating permanent while the
>   payment does (actionDispatcher.js:1545, costReservedPermanentIds): a "{1}, {T}:" creature ability with Phyrexian Altar as the only mana
>   and that creature its only victim is offered, then throws MANA_SHORT (measured with a probe card) — an offer/payment divergence, not
>   free mana. (3) Read, not reproduced: Purple Pentapus's tapped creature can still be planned as a mana source beside Cryptolith Rite, and
>   the tap cost then throws COST_UNPAYABLE (actionDispatcher.js:1365). (4) `manaUntapLine.availableMana` (manaUntapLine.js:85, an AI
>   estimate no legality reads) still sums two Altars sharing one victim twice.

>   (`spellEffects.parseSpellEffect`) read "… damage to target opponent" — and "… to target opponent or planeswalker" — as targetType
>   "player", the every-player pool, and that shape is the fallback every clause reaches through `parser.legacyToAtom`: spells, activated
>   and triggered abilities alike. The counters-put / counters-placed damage sentinels (`atoms/counters.js` — Shalai and Hallar, Casey
>   Jones) emitted "player" too. So Deadeye Duelist's ability was offered at `user` and `ai` both (a "target opponent" is never you — the
>   other player, CR 102.2; in a Free-for-All game every other player, CR 806.1 / 903.2; a target is chosen as the spell or ability is
>   put on the stack, CR 115.1, 601.2c, 602.2b), and so was every cast of Burning Fields, Jeskai Charm's damage mode, Vampiric Touch, and
>   the cast offer of a LOW spell (Stinging Vitriol). Triggers looked safe — the α1 chooser picks an enemy — but with every opponent
>   untargetable (Leyline of Sanctity) it found no correct-side candidate and `pickForcedTriggerCandidate` forced one from the pool: the
>   controller, where CR 603.3d removes the ability (probed: Shocking Sharpshooter, Shalai and Hallar and Casey Jones each dealt their
>   damage to their own controller, `trigger-target-forced: ["user"]`).

>   pool, `spellEffects.addOpponents`, which the discard / draw / life / mill / edict arms already use), "target player" → "player" as

>   controller (a pre-fix record, a saved game) now fizzles instead of dealing the damage (witnessed). The THAT-PLAYER rebind

> Committed on `day/spree`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The mechanic.** Spree means "Choose one or more modes. As an additional cost to cast this spell, pay the costs associated with those
>   modes" (CR 702.172a); a mode's cost is paid as the spell is cast when that mode is chosen, every chosen mode's cost (CR 700.2h). No parallel
>   modal path: `textNormalize.readSpree` reads the lead and the "+ {cost} — effect" lines all-or-nothing (the bare keyword, every later line a
>   mode, at least two, plain-mana costs only — hybrid / {X} / Phyrexian read nothing); `parseEffectProgramInner` re-reads the modes as the
>   existing "Choose one or more —" modal (parseModal's `atLeastOne`: every non-empty subset; each mode through the full clause machinery; one
>   unmodeled mode → LOW → the original parse, the card unchanged) and STAMPS `modal.spreeCosts` (printed order). The cast lane
>   (`legalChoices` program lane, `normalCast`, beside strive) charges the base cost — taxed and reduced as computed — plus the chosen modes'
>   costs as the action's own `cost` (CR 601.2f; the dispatcher pays that object, so offer and payment cannot drift), and offers only a set the
>   caster can fund; `expandCastChoices` already drops a mode whose targets can't be chosen (CR 700.2a) and `programAtoms` runs the chosen
>   modes in printed order (CR 608.2c). Mana value stays printed (CR 202.3). Not offered: under a free-cast permission (the dispatcher pays no
>   mana for `freeCast`, so the modes' costs could not be paid — every free-cast window has its own decline), and Fist of Suns' five-pip
>   variant is never twinned onto a cast carrying `spreeCost` (CR 118.9d). A generic reduction the base cost alone can't absorb is not carried
>   onto the modes' costs (an over-charge, never an under-charge).
> · **The AI** (`opponentAI.pickSpreeCast`, new policy key `spree`, 'v1' recovers the whole-card cascade): each chosen MODE is judged by the
>   hold it would face as a spell of its own — a counter mode only at an opponent's spell over the threat bar (`pickCounterCast`), a
>   change-target mode only as `pickChangeTargetCast`'s redirect, a wipe mode only when clearly behind, a team pump only when lethal, a fog only
>   when it saves the game, every target on its atom's side (`atomTargetIntent`; ambiguous never), "each creature target player controls" only
>   on a player with a creature — then the most modes, then the cheapest, then the heaviest permanent targets; none → hold. Placed before the
>   whole-card holds, which read every mode at once (Phantom Interference's counter mode would hold its token mode too).
> · **Three Steps Ahead's copy mode** — new `tokenCopy` arm: "Create a token that's a copy of target artifact or creature you control" →
>   copySource "target" over Teleportation Circle's `artifactOrCreatureYouControl` pool (the types it has now), Sagas kept out as Flash
>   Photography keeps them out (CR 714.3a); that enumeration branch now honours an atom's restrictions (its earlier carriers have none); the
>   atom's side is own (`atomTargetIntent`). A noncreature artifact copies (a Sol Ring token — witnessed).
> · **FIX (false positive): "Target player draws N cards and loses M life" names ONE player.** The DRAW-LOSE-SUBJECT normalize injected a
>   second "Target player" into the loss half, which parsed as a SECOND, independent player target: every cast offered the cartesian
>   (Sign in Blood in a 2-seat game: 4 casts, user-draws / ai-loses among them), and the trigger chooser drew for its controller while an
>   opponent lost the life (draw is own-side, lose-life enemy-side — re-proved on f71b7e86 for Bloodgift Demon's upkeep trigger). Now the
>   loss is a referent: the injection is the corpus-clean sentinel "the same target player", read by `atoms/life.js` as lose-life
>   `bindPreviousTargets` with no target of its own (CR 115.1; runProgram reads the draw's slice). 22 cards carry the shape (Sign in Blood,
>   Blood Pact, Painful Lesson, Harrowing Journey, Bloodgift Demon, Vault Plunderer, Fell Stinger, Unscrupulous Contractor, Shredder's
>   Revenge, Reverent Howl, Toil // Trouble, Cost of Brilliance, Wretched Confluence, Insatiable Avarice …); no tier moved; none is in the 30
>   profile decks. Graduated: `drawLoseSubject.test.js` (the loss atom is the bound referent now).
> · **Every Spree card's verdict** (text from the bundled oracle): native — Requisition Raid, Insatiable Avarice, Explosive Derailment,
>   Phantom Interference, Trash the Town, Three Steps Ahead. Parked, the blocking mode(s): **Great Train Heist** (#1118, Killer Turts) "+ {2}{R}
>   — Untap all creatures you control. If it's your combat phase, there is an additional combat phase after this phase." and "+ {R} — Choose
>   target opponent. Whenever a creature you control deals combat damage to that player this turn, create a tapped Treasure token."; **Return
>   the Favor** (#580) "+ {1} — Copy target instant spell, sorcery spell, activated ability, or triggered ability. …" (the copy-ability
>   resolver keeps the original's controller — right only for "an ability you control"); **Smuggler's Surprise** (#1582) "+ {2} — Mill four
>   cards. You may put up to two creature and/or land cards …" and "+ {1} — Creatures you control with power 4 or greater gain hexproof and

> · **The bug** (the Omnath self-play lane, measured on its deck: Nykthos games net −29 per ~868 vs about −10 expected). 3d121554's generic tap
>   promotes a plain colorless permanent (every record colorless, no rider), and each `planPaymentCore` call judged "plain" from the records it
>   was handed. Three passes hand it a subset: `planPaymentOnce`'s direct pass and `activateCostedInOrder`'s funding and rest calls see only the
>   records without an activation cost; `planPayment`'s pass A holds out the one-shot records; `planPaymentRemovalAware`'s pass A the counter
>   records. So Nykthos, Shrine to Nyx (its devotion line behind {2}) looked like Wastes and spent its tap on one {C} for generic before any
>   land; so did Three Tree City and, since f71b7e86 made their second lines, the filter lands and the "{1}, {T}: any color" lands; Crystal
>   Vein and Phyrexian Tower (their sacrifice line out of pass A — the side effect ebaca087 recorded) and storage lands holding counters.
> · **The fix.** `holdsBack(s)` — a record that is not plain and not spend-restricted. `planPayment` plans with each call's own judgment
>   (plan 1, byte-identical to before: 20,000 random boards, whole plans compared); when some permanent has a plain record beside a holdsBack
>   line (`boardJudgmentCanDiffer`) it plans again counting every holdsBack line on the whole list (plan 2 — the list rides as `board` through
>   the one-shot pass, the storage pass, the direct pass and the funding and rest calls) and returns plan 2 when it pays, else plan 1.
>   `canAfford` runs plan 1 alone. Carried: the planner's record builder is the named `plannerSourceRecord` (moved as is, plus f71b7e86's two
>   fields), `isPlainColorless` at module scope. An order change only (any mana pays generic, CR 107.4b).
> · **Why two plans (measured, not assumed).** The first build used plan 2 alone; a randomized differential (20,000 boards of real mana cards,
>   bundled oracle text, the f71b7e86 land lines included; random pool, cost and spend context) caught it moving affordability: 98 flips — 33
>   payable costs lost (Swamp, Mage-Ring Network, Simic Signet paying {U}{B}{G}: the funding call took the Swamp and stranded the {B}) and 65
>   found that the old order misses. The costed pass is greedy, and what its funding call taps decides the colors left for the rest. Shipped
>   planner: 0 of 20,000 disagree, 3,063 plans differ, 0 plans fail pool + taps − spend ≥ 0. The 65 boards stay unpayable on purpose (a safe
>   false negative kept, not a new offer; pinned: Selesnya Signet, Swamp, Cascading Cataracts can't pay {2}{C}).

>   own name read as "this aura", split quote-aware into sentences; each sentence is OWN (+N/+N incl. per-count and game-conditioned, a
>   keyword or protection, "can't be blocked", "can't be the target of spells", a granted activated ability — optional for its controller,
>   CR 602.1 —, a granted trigger whose effect is plainly a gain, umbra armor, its card returning when it dies, an extra mana or draw for its
>   controller, a +1/+1 counter or untap on it, an Aura-own activation that pumps or regenerates it, cost reductions for spells targeting it,
>   a land animated), ENEMY (−N/−N, can't attack / block / crew, abilities locked or costlier, doesn't untap, can't become untapped, loses
>   abilities / keywords / card types, defender, goad, attacks each combat, its controller losing life, dealt damage or sacrificing it,
>   destroyed / exiled for being damaged, targeted, tapped or blocking, tapped as the Aura enters, "you control enchanted …", a type set that
>   replaces its card types), NEUTRAL (the Aura's own business: Enchant, Flash, split second, cycling, vanishing / fading / cumulative upkeep
>   on the Aura, channel / forecast, a colour chosen, an enters draw / scry / life / investigate / exile or destroy of an opponent's
>   permanent, the Aura returning to hand, an upkeep cost), else UNKNOWN. Consensus: any UNKNOWN, or OWN beside ENEMY → null (hold); all
>   NEUTRAL → the side the Enchant line names ("… you control" own, "… an opponent controls" / "you don't control" enemy), else null. Two
>   rules above single clauses: a restriction beside a buff is MIXED here (the bonus reading calls it the buff's drawback — this reader never
>   trades a hold for a guess); a TRANSFORMATION ("loses all [other] abilities" / "all other card types") is ENEMY as a whole — the
>   abilities, base P/T and types the same sentence gives are the new body (Darksteel Mutation's indestructible 0/1, Kenrith's
>   Transformation's 3/3 Elk, Swift Reconfiguration's crew-5 Vehicle); a P/T change in it still counts. A condition on the host itself ("as
>   long as enchanted creature is white", "as long as it's a Human") is UNKNOWN. Cached per printed card. No tier, offer or resolution reads
>   it; the non-cast entry (`auraEntryIntent` → `chooseAuraEntryHost`, and the AI's flicker gain) reads the same answer, as designed.
> · **After (census, every Aura face, text from the bundled oracle):** body-only readable 623 → **289 read a side (172 own, 117 enemy)**, 334
>   held; all 1,274 Aura faces 445 → 774; **no existing reading changed** (the bonus parse is consulted first). Each of the 327 newly read
>   cards was reviewed by hand against its oracle text — no wrong side found. Neutral-only forced sides: Dying Wish, On Thin Ice,
>   Dimensional Exile, Chained to the Rocks, Ossification → own; Betrayal → enemy.
> · **Light-Paws Voltron (Omnath profile, 34 Auras).** Body-only — Angelic Destiny **own**, Benevolent Blessing **own**, Spectra Ward **own**,
>   On Thin Ice **own** (its snow land), Darksteel Mutation **enemy**, Swift Reconfiguration **enemy** (all six held before); native —
>   Chains of Custody **own**, Sheltered by Ghosts **own** (held before); All That Glitters, Daybreak Coronet, Eland Umbra, Ethereal Armor,

>   Gauntlets of Light (damage by toughness). **31 of 34 read a side (23 before).**
> · **The bug (false positive).** The native, Ordeal, bestow, mana-boost and granted-ability lanes enumerated hosts by targeting alone;
>   `canBeTargetedBy` reads protection from colours, not from enchantments, so Pacifism was offered on Azorius First-Wing ("Flying,
>   protection from enchantments" — it can't be targeted by enchantment spells, CR 702.16b, nor enchanted by enchantment Auras, CR 702.16c),
>   the AI cast it there, and AURA_ETB attached it. **The fix:** `auraSpellHost.enchantableHosts` (the body-only lane's last narrowing,
>   factored out) now narrows every Aura cast lane; AURA_ETB's resolution re-check asks `mayBeEnchantedBy` too (CR 608.2b, 608.3b — a
>   bestowed Aura whose target became illegal resolves as a creature, CR 702.103e). Animate Dead (a card in a graveyard) and the player lane
>   (players, not permanents) are outside it.
> · **And `mayBeEnchantedBy`'s printed-protection read** (auraEntry): it kept out any permanent whose text MENTIONED an unread protection, and
>   read multicolored / monocolored / colorless as unread. Measured by a spy-pilot A/B (each decision's offered Aura casts logged on both
>   trees), the first build of this slice withdrew LEGAL casts: Level Up and Shardmage's Rescue on Giver of Runes and Mother of Runes (they
>   grant protection to a target), mono-blue Ophidian Eye and Curiosity on Stonecoil Serpent (protection from multicolored). Now a protection
>   granted elsewhere — "target … gains", "you gain" (The One Ring), "enchanted … has" / "equipped creature has", "other creatures you
>   control" — is masked before the read, and the three colour-count qualities are read against the Aura's colours (CR 105.2a, 105.2b,
>   105.2c). Everything else still keeps the permanent out (fail closed: "this creature has / gains", "creatures you control have", "All
>   Slivers have"). Of the 59 permanents the old read kept out, 28 only grant protection elsewhere and may be enchanted again, the 6 with
>   protection from multicolored may wear a monocolored Aura and the 2 with protection from monocolored a multicolored one — in the
>   body-only lane and the non-cast entry too.
> · **A/B detail.** Pick changes: game 29 (Captain America casts Super-Soldier Serum on itself, held before) and games 60–69 (the Light-Paws
>   pod: Sheltered by Ghosts, Angelic Destiny, Benevolent Blessing, Spectra Ward, On Thin Ice, Swift Reconfiguration on Shorikai, Born to
>   Drive on Mobilizer Mech cast where they were held). Winners: games 60 and 65 Thrun → **Light-Paws** (Light-Paws 1 → 3 wins of its 10);
>   turn counts move in 60, 61, 62, 65, 66, 68, 69. Offered sets (the spy pilot, decision by decision until the trees' picks diverge): no

> · **Found, not fixed:** (1) an Aura whose only value is its enters exile (On Thin Ice, Chained to the Rocks, Dimensional Exile,

> · Witness **`auraClauseSide.test.js`** (28): the AI casts Angelic Destiny / Spectra Ward / Benevolent Blessing / Chains of Custody /

>   (`singleCastSpellFilter`: a card type, noncreature, historic, a colour, colorless, multicolored, a subtype); `spellMatchesFilter` matches any
>   item, with the every-creature-type flag (a changeling creature spell is a Dragon spell, CR 702.73a). No "and", no two-word item:
>   "multicolored instant or sorcery" (a conjunction) and "first instant or sorcery" stay unread. Twins, each audited whole-card: April O'Neil,
>   Human Element; Snake Pit; Mold Adder; God-Pharaoh's Faithful; Umara Wizard // Umara Skyfalls; Windrider Wizard; Alela, Artful Provocateur;
>   Rockslide Sorcerer; Umara Mystic.
> · **Lunar Mystic — a live FP closed on the way:** "an instant spell" read as `instantSorcery`, so its pay-{1}-draw fired on every sorcery.
>   "instant" and "sorcery" are their own filters now (CR 205.2a); the tier is unchanged (native-trigger).
> · **Visions of Beyond** — `interveningIf` reads "a graveyard has N or more cards in it": any seat in `state.players`, the caster's included
>   (CR 404.1); a player who left is gone from the map with their cards (CR 800.4a). The conditional-replacement arm already built draw 3 / draw 1;
>   the condition is read once as it resolves (the bundled ruling).
> · **Overmaster / Insist** — `nextSpellUncounterableClauseParser` reads "the next instant or sorcery spell …" and "the next creature spell …" as
>   the same atom with `spellFilter`; the resolver arms the filter on `player.nextTypedSpellUncounterable` (a set — arming twice is one shield);
>   `gameState.consumeTypedSpellShields` at the cast chokepoint consumes every filter the cast matches and stamps the stack object `uncounterable`,
>   leaving the others armed (a creature cast first does not use Overmaster's); the untap reset clears the list (only when present, so no seat's
>   state shape changes otherwise). The documented free-cast gap of the untyped flag applies here too.
> · **Vigor** — `combatEvasion.groupPreventPutCountersOf` (the two sentences as the whole line; a rider after them is another wall, not read and so
>   not enforced) and `groupPreventPutCounters` (another permanent the damaged creature's controller controls prints it), consulted at both funnels
>   beside the attached wall: combat (consultCombat → the after-step payout through addCounter) and `spellEffects.dealDamageToCreature` (inline).
>   "Another" and "you control" are pinned both ways; "Combat damage can't be prevented" (Frenzied Baloth) disables it in combat; two Vigors pay once.
>   A new coverage classifier strips the line whole and requires the rest keyword-only or fully covered (Vigor's trample and its shuffle trigger).
> · **Find // Finality** — Finality's "You may put two +1/+1 counters on a creature you control. Then all creatures get -4/-4 until end of turn."
>   Two cells: (1) the counter parser reads the untargeted "put N +1/+1 counters on a creature you control" as add-counter on the `oneYouControl`
>   scope (chosen as it resolves — the bundled ruling: not targeted, castable with no creature — by the shield-counter mode's house pick, the
>   highest-power creature; +1/+1 only); (2) `parseEffectClauseImpl` joins a "you may" sentence and a following bare "Then" sentence parsed apart —
>   the α2 suffix rule refuses optional-then-mandatory because "you may X and Y" is ambiguous, but a period and a bare "Then" make the scope plain
>   (CR 608.2c). Each half must parse HIGH alone and the second names nothing the first produced; consumers re-ask programConfidence of the joined
>   program, so a free cast first ("…without paying its mana cost. Then draw a card.") still parks. The join flipped nothing else in the corpus.
>   Twins, audited whole-card: Humiliate (the counter after the discard, chosen after the reveal — its ruling) and Sword of Truth and Justice.
> · **Gained, each witnessed on the real engine** (`firespitterWhelp.test.js` 21, `visionsOfBeyond.test.js` 5, `nextTypedSpellUncounterable.test.js` 8,
>   `vigorGroupPreventPutCounters.test.js` 14, `findFinality.test.js` 9): Firespitter Whelp — casting Divination and Shivan Dragon each takes every
>   opponent 40 → 39, a Bear deals nothing, a changeling counts; Visions — twenty cards in an opponent's or my own graveyard draws three, nineteen
>   everywhere draws one; Overmaster — the next instant is uncounterable and the one after is not, a creature first leaves the shield armed; Insist
>   the mirror; Vigor — a 3-damage hit on my Bears is three counters and no damage, Vigor itself and an opponent's creature take it, a 3/3 blocker
>   of a Hill Giant grows by three; Finality — taken, my Hill Giant survives as a 1/1 with two counters while the Bears and the Wurm die; declined,
>   everything dies; Humiliate — Divination discarded, then my Hill Giant gets the counter; the twins fire on a matching cast and not on another.
> · **AI play:** no policy changed. Veyran's Whelp now really burns the table on each noncreature cast, Visions really draws three late, Overmaster
>   really protects the next spell; Halfshell's Vigor really keeps its team alive and growing — but the AI's combat predictor does not read any
>   prevention wall (none of the walls are read there), so it still values blocks and attacks as if the damage lands; Mothman's Finality is a
>   native one-sided-ish sweeper the AI casts through its ordinary cast picker, with the counters going to its highest-power creature.
> · **Killer Turts — at 90, what holds the other ten:** Lion's Eye Diamond (a mana ability with a discard-your-hand cost that may be activated
>   only with priority, never inside a payment — needs a manual-only source the planner never taps, a discard-hand cost rider on the tap, and the
>   priority gate; the AI never takes manual taps, so it would stay inert for the AI), Scroll Rack (an any-number hand choice and an ordering),
>   Jeweled Amulet (the type of mana spent on the activation, stored and read back by the mana line), World War Hulk (chapter I's next-spell free
>   cast, chapter III's doubled P/T), Great Train Heist (spree), Last Night Together and World at War (extra combats with restrictions; rebound),
>   Tibalt's Trickery, Invasion of Ikoria (battles), Tezzeret, Cruel Captain (planeswalker — its own program).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** in combat the walls are consulted before the damage doublers, so Vigor's counters count the undoubled amount (the
>   noncombat funnel doubles first) — both are orders CR 616.1 lets the creature's controller choose; and the banked lone-blocker lethal cap
>   (preventDamagePutCounters.test.js) makes a 2/2 blocking a 3-power attacker earn two counters, not three. Stormwild Capridor (the self
>   noncombat form) and Phyrexian Hydra (-1/-1) are sibling sentences left unread.
